custom_fields.value: ***THE RADIO DECIDED 2026-10-04 (the user): Bluetooth Low Energy first***, *the one radio the T-Embed, the Pi Zero 2 W and every phone share; a slow beacon and an occasional scan for power. LoRa and the mesh stay C-16.* ***THE SERVER'S HALF BUILT 2026-10-04***: *a meeting is an interaction (`met`, species and an anonymous id); the next SYNC marks each met species SEEN in all three copies the game keeps (SaveBlock2's seen, SaveBlock1's seen1 and seen2 -- the game's anticheat believes only all three) and grows the carried daemon's friendship (+1 per companion met in a day, at most +5), its record decrypted, changed, re-summed and sealed (tests). The board's own beacon and scan are NOT built.* ***(the user, 2026-10-04 late)***: *the board's half waits for the phone app (C-27).* ***BUILT 2026-10-05 (the user: "build C-15 now so it's ready for later")***: *one beacon for every kind of companion -- a 128-bit service UUID, `dae0beac-0015-4d45-SSSS-PPPPPPPP0001`, the carried daemon's species and four random bytes new every hour, because a service UUID is the one thing an iPhone app may advertise. **The board** (`meet.cpp`): the beacon in its scan response, advertising kept on with the phone linked, a four-second listen every three minutes; a meeting is a flash and "A daemon nearby" (never a sound, never on a sleeping board), told to the server through a bridge (MET, BEACON lines) or over Wi-Fi, kept a while when there is neither. **The phone** (`app/beacon.ts`, a small native module `modules/daemons-beacon`): the same beacon, a five-second listen every three minutes while the app is open. **The server**: `POST /api/device/beacon` (our own tags, 48 hours) and `/api/device/met` (once an hour per tag, never one of ours -- so the board and the phone, which hear each other all day, never count), `GET /api/beacons`; the state names our tags so the board ignores the phone; DEVICE, ITS SETTINGS, MEET OTHERS NEARBY (on by default) (tests). What iOS allows: another iPhone is heard while its app is open; a board always. Built and installed; the board to be flashed; a real meeting waits for a second companion.* ***BOTH RADIOS PROVED 2026-10-05, with the user's own pair***: *the server records which of ours sent each tag and which heard it (our own are noted, never counted): the phone heard the board at once; the board heard NOTHING at all -- every listen started and reported zero devices, advertising on or paused -- because meet.cpp's scan callback and link.cpp's characteristic callback were both `class Heard`, and two classes of one name share one vtable at link time, so the scan called the link's callback. Renamed (`MeetListener`) and every callback class put in a file-local namespace; the next listen heard 57 devices and the phone's beacon, recorded as heard by the board. The board reports each listen (`LISTEN started devices beacons` -> `/api/device/listen`, shown in `/api/beacons`), so the radio can be checked from the companion. A real meeting waits for a second companion.* ***The final firmware (the three-minute listen) flashed 2026-10-06.***

custom_fields.value: ***2026-10-09***: *the Fire -- the DAC now runs only while a sound plays and GPIO 25 is held low between, as M5Unified holds it; if it still whines it is a module's (the LLM module has its own speaker). The watch -- macOS sees no USB device at all: LilyGO's note is that the port appears only once the crown is pressed a second (the PMU charges with the ESP32 off); and a real bug found: at 5% the firmware deep-slept waiting on BOOT, which the watch cannot press -- now it powers off through its PMU and the crown starts it. ***The CoreS3, found 2026-10-09***: *the firmware WAS on it -- each upload's RTS reset left it in download mode (asked without a reset, it answered as the bootloader); a watchdog reset (esptool 5's) started it, and it ran: HELLO as m5-cores3-e93368. `firmware/esp32/s3reset.py` (4.5.1's loader, esptool 5's registers) is now what updateCompanion.sh does to a silent native-USB board -- **not yet proven: its one try left the board silent**. Its boot lines also showed SensorLib refusing its touch ("Vendor id is 0x20 not match"): the CoreS3 has no touch yet -- to fix (read the FT6336 directly). ***2026-10-11, the CoreS3 on the cable again***: *flashed (C-93, C-94, C-98 and since) and it boot-looped: the ROM loaded the bootloader and it reset at once (rst 0x3, the same PC every time, inside the bootloader's image loading) -- a real power-off did not clear it. Found: the app at 0x10000 did NOT match the build (verify_flash: the bootloader, partitions and boot_app0 matched, the app's digest did not), though the upload had said "Hash of data verified". Written again with the RTC watchdog switched off first (reads had been cut off mid-way by a reset), checked by verify_flash, then s3reset.py: it ran -- `boot: screen CoreS3 SE`, `touch 1` (C-98's touch works), HELLO as m5-cores3-e93368, the watch face drawn (SHOT). So s3reset.py works on a good image; the loop was the bootloader refusing a bad one. Why the first write was bad is not known. Two lessons: after flashing an S3 over its own USB, run verify_flash; and shot.py's 15 s deadline is too short for the CoreS3's 320x240 (it took ~25 s).* ***The watch***: *no USB device at all, even in download mode, on two micro-USB cables -- most likely charge-only cables.*

issues.description: ~~**Every back view is checked to be a back** (*asked 2026-09-18*). **Several redrawn backs are front-like — the model turns a rear view to face the camera, or draws the same side view twice** — *flagged on the sheets so far: SENTRY, RAMROD, TRACER, STARR (following its concept), LATENCY, LULL, NOZZLE, STUB, HANDLER; and batch 12's COLDREAD, HAUNTPROC and TRACKER; batch 13's MULTICAST; batch 14's BLINDSPOT, WHIM, HUDDLE, FIXATION, SIMMER, OMEN and BRISTLE (side-on or facing); batch 15's VIGILANCE, GRASP, IMITATION, REPAY and ILLUSION.* ***The job***: **one contact sheet of every redrawn daemon's front beside its back, read by eye, and a list of the failures** — *then each failure redrawn with batch 7's rear wording ("seen from directly behind, no face visible, back of the head") and a face-and-eyes negative, several seeds, and rebuilt.* *A check a tool can make first: a back whose pixels correlate too closely with its own front (a mirrored or duplicated view) is suspect.* ***Closes when every back on the sheet reads as the creature from behind, and the list is empty.*** ***AUDITED AND A FIRST PASS DRAFTED 2026-09-19*** (*`gfx/drafts/t166/`*): **the audit (`audit_*.png`, `similarity.txt`) found 67 front-like backs, not the 25 listed** — *the symmetric daemons (CLUSTER, LOCUS, BEACON, PULSAR, the jellyfish, dragonflies, crabs) are right to match and are left alone.* **All 67 redrawn back-only, three seeds each (201 drafts); 21 are good rear views of the same creature (`picks.json`, `sheet.png`) — approved and BUILT 2026-09-19 (engine `c97d80a44`), 46 left for the second pass.** ***SECOND PASS BUILT 2026-09-19*** (engine `1748b65c5`; *`second.py`, `picks2.json`, `sheet2.png`, approved; building it found PING's back had been made from its old Gemini JPEG since batch 2, because `gbasprite.py` took the first file its glob matched — it now prefers the PNG*): **each described from its APPROVED front, fish, seahorses and serpents asked for a three-quarter rear view; 20 more are good** — *CHILLER, ENSEMBLE, FERRY, HAUNTPROC, INFERENCE, PING, PIPELINE, RAMROD, RESENTMENT, REVENANT, SENTINEL, SMOGSTACK, WISP, WILDFIRE, WHIM, BLINDSPOT, SEEDLING, SPAWN, FOSSILNET, GRIEVANCE.* **26 remain and are the hard core**: *the owls (COLDREAD, VIGILANCE), the seahorses (NOZZLE, JETSTREAM, TURBULENCE), most fish (BRISTLE, STUB, UPSTREAM), the deer (ILLUSION, STARR), the horses (HOTPATH, OVERDRIVE), and APATHY, BROADCAST, CRYOGEN, EMERGENCE, ESCALATE, FIXATION, GRASP, HANDLER, IMITATION, OMEN, REPAY, SIMMER, SINGULAR, AXIOMKICK* — **the model draws them facing, side-on or as a different creature however they are asked.** *The likely way through is image-to-image from the approved FRONT, mirrored, at a low denoise with a rear-view prompt — keeping the body and turning only the head away — or a hand edit that removes the face.* ***THIRD PASS TRIED 2026-09-19 and it FAILED*** (*`third.py`, `alt3/`*): **image-to-image from each approved front, mirrored, at 0.45/0.55/0.65 with a rear-view prompt, redraws the mirrored front at every strength — the face comes back each time; 0 of 78 turned.** ***What is left, and it is two different problems***: **13 are SIDE-ON daemons whose mirrored side view already faces the foe** (*NOZZLE, JETSTREAM, TURBULENCE, STUB, UPSTREAM, HOTPATH, OVERDRIVE, ILLUSION, STARR, HANDLER, EMERGENCE, ESCALATE, FIXATION*) — *accepting that as the back is what many Gen 3 sprites do;* **13 are FACE-ON daemons with no back the model will draw** (*COLDREAD, VIGILANCE, BRISTLE, APATHY, BROADCAST, CRYOGEN, GRASP, IMITATION, OMEN, REPAY, SIMMER, SINGULAR, AXIOMKICK*) — *they need a drawn back concept, a hand edit, or a different model.* ***THE LAST 26, SPLIT 2026-09-19*** (*decided by the user; `fourth.py`, `clean4/`, `sheet3.png`, approved and built*): **the 13 side-on daemons take their approved front MIRRORED as the back; the 13 face-on take the mirrored front with the face removed in code** — *eyes, beak and mouth are the dark or saturated pixels inside the head's outline, filled from the body around them.* *APATHY also lost its dark spots and reads washed-out; IMITATION keeps a trace of its eyes.* ***Why only 21, and what the second pass needs***: *the prompts reused each batch's FIRST description, not the redraw that was approved — so COLDREAD came back a woman, ENSEMBLE palm trees, HANDLER a blue duck, PIPELINE a humanoid. Fish, seahorses, ghosts and serpents also resist a rear view at all.* **Second pass: describe each from its APPROVED front (what is actually drawn), and for the fish and serpents accept a mirrored three-quarter view as the back, which is what the source games did.** *Six more cleaned badly and were dropped (CHILLER, INFERENCE, GRASP, REPAY, IMITATION, OMEN), and SENTINEL's new back still showed its eye.*~~ — ***Done 2026-09-19*** (engine `dca915c11`): **all 67 front-like backs fixed — 21 and 20 redrawn as true rear views (passes one and two), 13 side-on mirrored and 13 face-on de-faced (the user's split).** *APATHY reads washed-out and IMITATION keeps a trace of its eyes; both are candidates for a hand-drawn back later.*

issues.description: ~~**Every overworld sprite and tile redrawn through the sprite server, in batches** (*asked 2026-09-18*). **The world art so far — buildings, ground, nature tiles, people, the player (T-52, T-61–T-85, T-105–T-129) — was generated in CODE by the `gba*`/`gen*` tools; the daemons are now drawn through ComfyUI on roverbyteseer (`spriteforge.py`, pixelbyte's model), and the world should be too.** ***The job, planned like T-131***: **a census of every overworld sheet and tileset (object events, trainer overworlds, primary and secondary tilesets, the ones already ours included), then batches in the order a player sees them, each drafted, on a contact sheet, approved, then built** — *tiles are a harder target than sprites: 8×8 cells, shared palettes per tileset, metatile layers and collision that must not move (T-125's zero-collision-change rule), and seams between tiles (engine.md trap 14).* ***Depends on T-133*** *for the daemon objects.* **First step: a trial on one building and one ground tileset, to learn whether the model can draw tileable 16×16 metatiles at all, before a plan is written.** ***TRIAL DONE 2026-09-19*** (*`gfx/drafts/t164/trial/`: `make.py`, `judge.py`, `sheet.png`, `restyle_strengths.png`*) — **the answer is split, and it decides the plan.** **(1) From words the model cannot author a tileset**: *asked for a house it draws a whole VIGNETTE (yard, trees, a border) and one of three in isometric perspective; asked for grass it draws hedgerows and crop rows. The best 16×16 grass crop does tile (seam ratio 0.09) but reads as a field, not ground.* **(2) Restyling the CURRENT art keeps the layout, and there is a sweet spot**: *at 0.35–0.50 it hands back the original with softer shading; at 0.65 a real improvement with the SAME footprint (warmer walls, wooden trim, roof and windows where they were); at 0.80 it redesigns — dormers, a door, windows moved — which would move collision.* **(3) Ground should stay generated in code**: *restyled at any strength, grass grows invented objects (flowers, fences, signs) and stops tiling.* ***So the plan***: **buildings get a restyle pass at ~0.6 from the code-drawn art, then are quantized back to their tileset's palettes and re-cut into 8×8 tiles with collision untouched; ground, paths, water and nature stay with the `gba*`/`gen*` tools; overworld PEOPLE and objects are sprites and go through the sprite recipe that drew the daemons.** ***Next step, a pilot***: *one real building end to end — restyle its metatiles as rendered, quantize to the tileset's own palettes (one palette per 8×8 tile), re-cut, check the tile budget and that no collision moved, build, and look at it in the game.* ***PILOT DONE 2026-09-19*** (engine `967863e4d`; `tools/gbarestyle.py`, `gfx/drafts/t164/pilot/`): **Doldrum's house, end to end, in the game.** *What the pilot found*: **(1) houses are a shared KIT** — *the left house's blocks and 27 tiles also build Doldrum's other houses, and the tileset had 33 free tile slots, so the restyle rewrites the kit's tiles IN PLACE and every house made of them changes together (a town that matches);* **(2) a palette row had to be freed** — *none was spare; row 7's four colours moved into row 10's unused slots, and the kit was redrawn in row 7;* **(3) the model SATURATES** — *Doldrum's muted roofs came back bright cyan and the pillars bright green, so `--keep-colour` keeps the restyle's LIGHTNESS and takes each pixel's hue and chroma from the house as it was.* **The result is modest and faithful**: *crisper roof ribs, a stone plinth along the wall base, the town's own colours; roofs a touch lighter.* ***Nothing structural moved*** — *block ids, collision, the door and the map are untouched; four ROMs build; seen in the game beside THE REPO.* ***The decision this leaves for the user***: **whether the gain is worth a pass over every town's kit** (each needs its own free row, and the model's saturation means `--keep-colour` is the default), **or whether T-164's effort goes to the overworld PEOPLE and objects, where the sprite recipe already works well.** ***PEOPLE AND OBJECTS TRIED 2026-09-19*** (*decided by the user: people and objects over buildings; `gfx/drafts/t164/people/`: `trial.py`, `judge.py`, `sheet.png`*): **the model has little to add at overworld scale.** **People**: *a whole 9-frame 16×32 sheet restyled at once keeps the walk cycle one character — but at 0.40 it hands back the original and at 0.55 it adds only speckle; a 16×32 frame has no room for the detail the model brings to a 64px daemon.* **Objects from words**: *hit or miss at 16×16 — the fossil (an ammonite) and the Lapras doll read; the signs keep a dark frame and the town map is a blob.* ***Conclusion, measured three ways (buildings, people, objects)***: **the sprite server's strength is the 64px battle sprite; at the overworld's 16px scale the `gba*`/`gen*` code tools, which drew the fable cast, remain the right instrument.** *What is actually left as vanilla on the overworld, by pixel against upstream AND checked for use*: **no people** — *CAMERAMAN, RICH BOY, SITTING BOY and STREAM's host are still vanilla's pixels, but no map places them and no script or code creates them (CAMERAMAN and RICH BOY are not even in the pointer table; RICH BOY lives on only as a trainer class, whose PORTRAIT is T-120's); the first report of "four people a player meets" matched pixels without checking use, and was wrong* — **and thirteen objects, every one of them shown** (*T-167*).~~ — ***Closed 2026-09-19, the question answered***: **the sprite server is the instrument for 64px battle sprites and not for the overworld's 16px world** — *measured on buildings (a faithful but modest kit restyle, which stays in Doldrum), people (whole-sheet restyles add only noise) and objects (hit or miss at 16×16). The world stays with the `gba*`/`gen*` code tools; what is left of vanilla there is T-167.*

issues.description: ~~**The streaks, in the engine**~~ — ***Engine done 2026-09-17*** (engine `8a46d4b07`; `tools/genstreaks.py`, `tools/gbasprite.py`) (*9.4, amended 2026-09-17, v11.209*). **A daemon's palette indices 11–14 are filled from the types of the four moves it knows, whenever a real daemon is shown; the species palette ships them grey.** ***Measured***: *27 calls across 11 files choose a daemon's palette — `battle_gfx_sfx_util.c` 6, `evolution_scene.c` 5, `trainer_pokemon_sprites.c` 3, `trade_scene.c`, `pokemon_storage_system_data.c`, `pokemon.c`, `daycare.c` and `battle_anim_mons.c` 2 each, and one each in `pokemon_special_anim_scene.c`, `pokemon_jump.c` and `field_effect.c`* — **and every one returns a COMPRESSED palette from ROM chosen by species and shininess, so the patch has to happen AFTER the load, in the palette buffers, not in the lookup.** ***The work***: **one function that takes a palette offset and a daemon and writes 11–14 from its moves' types** (*each type's LIGHT step, generated into a C header from `gbasprite.py`'s `TYPE_COLOR` so the two cannot drift; an empty slot takes the body's mid step*), **called after each load that can see a daemon**; *`PERSPECTIVE` copies the target's streaks because it copies the target's moves.* **`gbasprite.py` learns the four marker colours and writes 11–14 grey.** ***Not blocked on art***: *it can be built and proved on an existing sprite whose drawing has streak regions added — the first real test is a daemon in battle whose four moves are four different types, and the same species in the Index, blank.* **Icons cannot carry it (three shared palettes)** ***Built***: *`src/daemon_streaks.c` writes 11–14 from a daemon's moves at every load that can see one — battle (before either palette load), the ghost unveiled, `PERSPECTIVE` (the target's moves), move-animation copies, storage (party and box), hatching, trade, all five evolution loads, the item/TM scene, the summary, and field moves (found in the party by personality and OT); the Index, Hall of Fame and link minigame see only a species and stay grey, which is the rule.* ***The rail, and how its first version was the hazard***: **a species is touched only if the build marked its palette — the one blank grey in all four of 11–14 — because a vanilla palette uses all sixteen colours**; *the first flag counted any sprite drawing with 11–14 and found 346, every vanilla daemon, and it ran in report mode first.* ***The streak step is per BODY and MOVE type***: **light, or dark where the light one vanishes — 28 of 324 pairs** (*v11.210 corrected 9.4's "reads as a vein", which the preview disproved*). ***And a bug older than the streaks***: **`gbasprite.py` wrote each palette from the BACK, so DEADLOCK's badge was black in battle and two of PING's accents with it** — *one palette per species now.* ***Not yet seen in the game***: **no species has streak art, so today nothing on screen changes; the in-battle check — four moves of four types, and the same species grey in the Index — is T-131's first batch's acceptance test.**

objects at 16×16 are hit or miss; ground grows invented objects and stops tiling* — **so the world stayed with the `gen*` code tools.** ***This ticket asks whether a DIFFERENT METHOD changes that***: **draw each character at 64px through spriteforge, the scale it is good at, and REDUCE it to the 16×32 walk sheet in code** — *keeping the frame count, the NPC palette slot (trap 17) and the walk cycle, so only the drawing changes.* ***First step is a trial, not a redraw***: *three sheets (a person, a Clear, a leader), reduced and put beside the code-drawn ones in the game; `gfx/drafts/t170/`: `make.sh`, `from_portraits.png`, `from_overworld_shape.png`): **a 64px drawing does not survive the reduction to a 16x32 frame, and it was asked twice.** ***First, from the portraits***: *the reduced YOUNGSTER, CRYSTAL and TILT lose the outline entirely, the head comes out a fraction of the frame, and the figure reads as a smear beside the code-drawn frame beside it -- an overworld figure is about two heads tall and a portrait is not.* ***Then, asking for the overworld's own shape at 64px*** (*chibi, two heads tall, huge head, thick black outline, flat colour -- the thing a 16x32 frame is actually made of*): **better, and still not usable** -- *the outline breaks up, the flats turn to speckle, and every one is beaten by the frame we have.* ***The reason is structural, which is why no third prompt was tried***: **a 16-pixel-wide figure is about ten pixels of body, and every one of them is placed on purpose** -- *a downscale averages, and averaging is exactly what destroys an outline and a flat.* **The `gen*` code tools place each pixel; issues.description: ~~**Is every daemon a thing that RUNS?** (*asked by the user 2026-09-20*). **The game is called DAEMONS, and a daemon is a process that runs in the background** — *`PING`, `FORK`, `THREAD`, `MUTEX`, `SEMAPHORE`, `SCHEDULER`, `TRACER`, `SENTINEL`, `ROOTKIT` and `SPAWN` all are.* ***But some of ours are a CONDITION a running system is in, not a thing that runs***: **`DEADLOCK`, `LIVELOCK`, `LATENCY`, `OVERFLOW`, `HEAP`, `STACK`, `FAULT`, `STATIC`, `RESIDUAL`** — *the user's own example is DEADLOCK.* **The user is explicit that this is not being proposed as a rule**: *the job is to MEASURE how many do not fit the mould, and only then to ask whether any should change.* ***What the review must not flatten*** — **8.2b already ruled three registers and they are deliberate**: *the ISLANDS' daemons are psychology (APATHY, DREAD, TRUST, HOPE, GRIEVANCE, VALENCE — Act 2 is mind), the legendaries are myth (ASCLEPIUS, ORPHEUS, PROMETHEUS), and MUSAI, ROVER and PIXELBYTE → REFORGE are the project's own.* **So the question is asked of KANTO's bestiary, which is the technical register, and the others are counted apart rather than judged.** ***The job***: **classify all 229 renamed species into (a) a thing that runs, (b) a thing a running system HAS or DOES, (c) a state it is IN, (d) psychology, (e) myth, (f) ours** — *a small tool, so the count can be re-run rather than re-argued* — **then a table of the Kanto names that are not (a) or (b), each with what it would become if it changed, and what that costs.** ***And the cost is real***: *a species rename sweeps prose (`port_vocab`), rewrites Index entries (8.2c), and 8.2b's own trap says **name tables are authored, prose is swept** — so a rename is never only a name.* ***COUNTED 2026-09-20*** (`tools/checkregister.py`, every judgement written down in it; a name missing from the table is reported, never guessed): **of 151 KANTO names — RUNS 31, DOES 16, HAS 42, STATE 19, WORLD 31**, *plus MYTH 3 and OURS 9 by 8.2b's ruling; beyond Kanto, MIND holds 26.* ***So 50 of 151 are not processes — but the two groups fail differently.*** **The 19 STATE names are still COMPUTING words** (*deadlock, livelock, latency, spaghetti, stampede*): *they fit the lexicon and not the stricter rule, and 8.2b's own ruling asks for the technical SURFACE rather than for processes — DEADLOCK and LIVELOCK are also a deliberate pair, which a rename would break.* **The 31 WORLD names split three ways**: *(a) logic and rhetoric — PROOF, THEOREM, CONJECTURE, REBUTTAL, CANON, RUBRIC, LEMMA MIND, LOCUS, VICE — which read as the LOGIC type's own register; (b) nature and weather — BLIGHT, WEED, SEEDLING, WILDFIRE, JETSTREAM, PULSAR, SLUDGE, FUMES, WISP, CRYOGEN — the ten genuinely outside the lexicon; (c) machines and creature-parts — BULLDOZER, RAMROD, NOZZLE, CHILLER, PINCER, CLAMPJAW, MITE, CAIRNLING, RELIC, REVENANT, HUNCH, TRANCE.* ***The recommendation put to the user***: **leave the states, treat (a) as deliberate, and rule on (b) — about ten names — and (c).** ***(b) RENAMED 2026-09-20, approved*** (engine `55ad1ed5d`): **WEED → SPRAWL, BLIGHT → SKEW, SLUDGE → DEADLETTER, FUMES → EXHAUST, WISP → DANGLING, WILDFIRE → OVERRUN, PULSAR → CRON, JETSTREAM → BACKPRESS, CRYOGEN → ARCHIVER, SEEDLING → CANARY.** *Each was checked against every name surface first — SNAPSHOT, RUNAWAY, ZOMBIE, ORPHAN and SPILLOVER were the first choices and all five are already an item, a move or an ability.* ***The Index entries needed nothing***: **they already describe the process rather than the creature** (*GRIMER's says nothing was thrown away, it was all kept somewhere nobody decided on — which IS a dead-letter queue*), *which is why the names could move at all.* ***What the rename cost***: **two lines of dialogue** (*SilphCo 5F names the KOFFING line, CINNABAR's gym names NINETALES*) **and twenty drawings renamed so `gbasprite.py` still finds them** — *179px and 159px, and 1722 lines in the game are already wider.* ***Honest about what it achieved***: *the ten left WORLD, but only CRON, ARCHIVER and CANARY became things that RUN; six are conditions, which is what those daemons are. Kanto WORLD 31 → 21.* ***SPAGHETTI RULED ON 2026-09-20 — KEPT*** (*the user asked after the rename; the entry was read before the ruling*): **it passes the test the ten failed** — *spaghetti code is a term of art, so the name is INSIDE the lexicon; it sits in the same bucket as DEADLOCK, which is already ruled to stay.* ***The reason to hesitate was that it reads as a JOKE first***, *and a laugh is louder than a wrong category — 8.2b files it under craft rule 6, the joke is allowed to sit underneath and is never pointed at.* ***The entry earns it***: **TANGELA's Index entry is `TANGLED` — "Every part of it reaches every other part. Nobody who could explain it is still here."** — *a plain description of tangled code and of legacy nobody can account for, which never mentions pasta; the second sentence is about the people who are gone.* **And the word appears NOWHERE else in the game** — *no dialogue, no sign, no other entry — so nothing in play points at it.* ***If it ever stops feeling earned the name is a one-line change and the entry needs nothing.*** ***Closes when*** *the count exists and the user has ruled on each name that does not fit.*~~ — ***RULED ON (a) AND (c), 2026-09-20*** (engine `14f096e70`; the user asked for the ruling): **(a) the logic and rhetoric names are KEPT — PROOF, THEOREM, LEMMA MIND, CONJECTURE, REBUTTAL, CANON, RUBRIC, LOCUS, and HUNCH with them.** *They are the LOGIC and CONTEXT types' OWN register (2.2: LOGIC is symbolic rules, brute force, proof), their entries are process descriptions, and HUNCH → INFERENCE → CONJECTURE is one line about reasoning — arriving at the answer without passing through the working, then stating what it cannot prove. Formal logic is technical vocabulary, not a stray.* ***Two corrections the entries forced***: **VICE was never a logic name** (*KINGLER: closes with more force than it can control*) **and HUNCH was never a machine** — *the grouping came from the words, the ruling came from the entries.* **(c) the machines and creature-parts: TWELVE RENAMED, each from what its own entry says.** *RAMROD → HARDCODE (picks a direction and then stops picking), BULLDOZER → MIGRATE (moves ground from where it was to where it is wanted), NOZZLE → BOTTLENECK (narrow enough to raise the pressure) → BACKPRESS, CHILLER → HEATSINK (draws heat out and keeps it) → ARCHIVER, PINCER → ACQUIRE → VICE → LOCKUP (takes a hold, then will not release), CLAMPJAW → BLOCKING (does not reopen until the thing stops moving), MITE → RESIDENT (already inside before anyone looks, and a resident program is one that stays) → SPYWARE, RELIC → ARTEFACT and CAIRNLING → COREFILE (what is left when something stops, carried and never put down), REVENANT → RESPAWN (ended twice; both times something started it again) between DANGLING and HAUNTPROC, TRANCE → BUSYWAIT (holds attention on one point until nothing else is running).* ***What it cost***: **eight files of prose swept, including the tower's** (*'I saw ARTEFACT's mother die trying to' — 204px, and vanilla's own widest dialogue line is over 300*), **and VENONAT's category was RESIDENT, which would have been its name too: now UNNOTICED.** — ***Closed 2026-09-20***: **Kanto WORLD 31 → 9, and the nine are the logic register, kept on purpose.** *RUNS 35, DOES 19, HAS 48, STATE 28 — the states stay, by the first ruling, and SPAGHETTI with them.*

six bodies made processes (held state was read, suspended and came back clear, THRASHING from the work, queued to suspend, idled, is clear); and the two phrasings — CURSE reflowed to 'cut its own HP / and CONSULTED {DEF}' and STARVATION's article, 'was left in STARVATION'.* ***Every line measured against the one it replaces***, *worst case being `Remote ` plus a ten-character nickname — the model reproduces engine.md's published 145px for `sText_AttackerUsedX` exactly — and **none is wider**: CURSE's pre-existing overflow drops 424px to 190px against the 196px box.* ***And the five surfaces nobody was looking at***: **the quest log taught CUT, FLY and DIG and named ROCK TUNNEL and VICTORY ROAD** — *now PRUNE, GOTO, EXCAVATE, THE BLACKOUT and UMBRAL ASCENT, with 'flew to' becoming 'went to' and 'escape from' becoming 'leave'.* — ***Closed 2026-09-20***: **`check_lexicon.py` exits 0 again — the gate this ticket left red is green**, *and all four ROMs build.*

issues.description: ~~**A second type-name table nobody swept — and one entry names the wrong thing** (*found by T-172's detector, 2026-09-20*). **`sATypeMove_Table` in `battle_message.c` is eighteen strings of the form `a FLYING move`, and it is a SEPARATE copy of the type names from `gTypeNames`** — *read by `ChooseTypeOfMoveUsedString`, so a player meets it whenever a routine's type has to be said aloud.* ***Sixteen of the eighteen are still vanilla's***: **NORMAL, FIGHTING, FLYING, GROUND, ROCK, BUG, GHOST, STEEL, FIRE, WATER, GRASS, ELECTRIC, ICE, DRAGON, DARK and `???`** — *while `gTypeNames` has called them CONTENT, LOGIC, VECTOR, STRATUM, LEGACY, SWARM, LATENT, HARDENED, ENTROPY, FLOW, GROWTH, SIGNAL, FROZEN, EMERGENT, OPAQUE and ORACLE since 2.6.* ***Only two were ever converted, and one of those is WRONG***: **`gText_APoisonMove` correctly says CORRUPT; `gText_APsychicMove` says CONSTRUE, and the CONTEXT type is called CONTEXT** — *CONSTRUE is the trainer class and the CONTEXT routine, which is the same double this very file's collision check was extended for. A line that names a type by another thing's name is worse than one that is simply stale.* ***Why this is its own ticket and not part of T-172***: **invariant 3 and invariant 6.** *The type chart is the argument, and renaming type CONSTANTS is ruled expensive and optional — but this is neither: these are STRINGS, and the decision that `gTypeNames` should read CONTENT and VECTOR was made in 2.6 and applied. This table is that decision, unapplied. Bringing it into line changes no constant and no chart.* ***Still to settle***: *whether the article survives the rename* — **`an ELECTRIC move` becomes `a SIGNAL move` and `a GHOST move` becomes `a LATENT move`, so `gText_AnElectricMove` and `gText_AnIceMove` change article while others do not** — *and what `a ??? move` should read as, ORACLE being a real type here rather than vanilla's placeholder.* ***Closes when*** *all eighteen agree with `gTypeNames`, the articles are right, and `make -C engineGba firered` exits 0.*~~ — ***DONE AND CLOSED 2026-09-20*** (engine `a43cf6660`): **all eighteen agree with `gTypeNames` now**, *checked pair by pair rather than by eye.* ***The two open questions, settled by the sentence they land in***: **the log reads `{ATTACKER} invoked\na VECTOR routine`** — *so the string says ROUTINE, as the menus and T-138's descriptions do, and the ARTICLE follows OUR word: an ORACLE, an ENTROPY, an EMERGENT, an OPAQUE, and `a SIGNAL routine` where vanilla had `an ELECTRIC move`.* **`a ??? move` is `an ORACLE routine`** — *ORACLE is a real type here (2.6), not vanilla's placeholder.* *The C SYMBOLS keep vanilla's spelling (`gText_AnElectricMove` holds "a SIGNAL routine"); renaming them is churn and changes nothing a player sees.* ***And the reason this happened is now checked***: **`check_lexicon.py` compares the two copies every run** — *`the battle log's type names agree with the chart's`, and breaking one on purpose prints `TYPE_FLYING 'a FLYING routine', and gTypeNames says VECTOR`.* **A copy nobody checks is how the log came to name a type that exists nowhere else in the game.**
issues.subject: T-173 A second type-name table nobody swept — and one entry names the wrong thing

issues.description: ~~**R in battle = PERSPECTIVE** (*held open by T-179, taken up by the user the same day*). **9.2's move is *become another thing for a while*; this is the same idea offered as a LOOK.**~~ — ***DONE AND CLOSED 2026-09-20*** (engine; `battle_controller_player.c`; 4.2, v11.227): **R on the action menu redraws the fight from where the opponent stands** — *their back where your daemon stands, your daemon's face where theirs was, both from art every species already has* — **and R or B puts it back.** ***The picture is the hook; the INFORMATION is the argument***: **the two windows become two accounts side by side — THEIR hit points TO THE NUMBER, YOURS only as a shape** (*untouched, marked, hurt, badly hurt, barely up*). *That is what each side actually knows, and nothing says so.* ***Decided with the user***: **it costs nothing** — *charging for a perspective would make a player ration the one thing this game keeps asking them to do* — **and it shows the fight and what each side knows, not what the opponent INTENDS**, *which would turn a perspective into an oracle.* ***Built INSIDE the battle*** (*the live sprites and healthboxes hidden, two pic sprites created opposite*), **because the Index's teardown would have meant rebuilding the whole battle to show a still of it.** ***Three engine facts it turned up***: **`CreatePicSprite` only assigns a sprite's `paletteNum` when the tag is `TAG_NONE`** — *handed a real tag it keeps whatever the shared template last had, which drew both daemons as black silhouettes; the slots are reserved through the palette manager now* — **`B_WIN_MSG` is not drawn at all while an action is being chosen** (*two attempts printed into nothing*), **and the prompt box is about eleven characters wide**, *so a sentence clipped to "ROVERCUB has 118 of".*
issues.subject: T-180 R in battle = PERSPECTIVE

issues.description: ~~**L and R do nothing, and the game has uses for them** (*asked by the user 2026-09-20, after the debug menu's own L/R were found dead*). ***What is already true***: **BUTTON MODE has three settings — `HELP`, `LR`, `L=A` — and vanilla gave the DEFAULT slot to the Help System**, *so L and R open a help tab everywhere instead of doing the paging `LR` mode already implements in the summary screen, the Index and the storage boxes.* **The useful behaviour shipped and was switched off.** ***Decided with the user***: **(1) `LR` becomes the default**, *so every menu gets paging immediately*; **(2) `L` = READ** — *the Index entry for whatever is on screen: the daemon in battle, in the party, or standing in front of you* — **which is the one the design wants**: *4.2 makes the Index the artifact that can only measure content, and a button that pulls the record up mid-fight makes that inadequacy present rather than three menus away;* **(3) `R` = AGAIN** — *repeat the last line, because FRLG has no dialogue history and a mistimed A loses a line permanently in a game this dense with writing;* **(4) the HELP System moves into the START menu as an entry**, *so nothing is lost and it stops owning two buttons.* ***Held as an open question, not part of this ticket***: **`R` held in battle = PERSPECTIVE** — *9.2's move is 'become another thing for a while', and holding R would show the fight from the opponent's side, their HP as they read it and your daemon's streaks from behind.* **It is the game's subject as a button and it is a second battle layout plus a rule about what it costs.** ***Closes when*** *LR is the default, L and R carry READ and AGAIN in the field, the party and battle, HELP is reachable from the menu, and the options text says what the buttons do.* ***THREE OF THE FOUR DONE 2026-09-20*** (engine, `start_menu.c`, `option_menu.c`, `help_system_util.c`, `field_message_box.c`, `field_control_avatar.c`, `overworld.c`, `stream.inc`): **LR is the default, HELP is a START menu entry, and R says the last line again** — *verified in play: R repeats "The ferry at ARDOR PORT is running.", twice; the HELP entry opens and returns to the menu.* ***Three things the work found that the ticket had not***: **(a) the start menu's DESCRIPTIONS were gated on HELP mode too** — *"A device that records DAEMON secrets upon meeting or binding" is our writing, and LR mode silently lost it; the condition is gone;* **(b) HELP stops being a BUTTON MODE at all** — *with the menu as the door, a mode whose whole content was "L and R open a help tab" would mean "L and R do nothing", so OPTIONS offers LR and L=A and a save still holding HELP is moved on when it continues AND when the start menu opens* (**the first migration sat on a callback the CONTINUE path does not take**, *which is why the save kept opening a help tab*); **(c) R = AGAIN had become DEBUG-ONLY by accident** — *its include, its string and its script each landed inside a `#if DAEMONS_DEBUG` block, so the two RELEASE ROMs would not compile.* **Found by building all four rather than the one being tested, which is the habit this project already has a trap written for.** ***STILL OPEN: `L` = READ***, *the Index entry for whatever is on screen — the biggest of the four, because the Index is its own overlay and calling it from a battle means saving and restoring that state.*~~ — ***DONE AND CLOSED 2026-09-20*** (engine; `start_menu.c`, `option_menu.c`, `help_system_util.c`, `field_message_box.c`, `field_control_avatar.c`, `overworld.c`, `pokedex_screen.c`, `battle_controller_player.c`, `stream.inc`; 4.2, v11.226): **all four done and verified in play.** ***`LR` is the default***, *so the paging vanilla already implemented in the Index, the summary screen and the boxes is switched on.* ***HELP is a START menu entry*** (*"What the game will tell you about itself."*) — **and no longer a button mode at all**, *since with the menu as the door a mode whose whole content was "L and R open a help tab" would mean "L and R do nothing".* ***`R` = AGAIN***, *the last line said again, kept as EXPANDED text because a script's message is built in `gStringVar4` from buffers that have moved on.* ***`L` = READ***: **the opposing daemon's Index entry from the battle action menu, and B returns to the fight with both sprites, both healthboxes and the menu intact.** *`DexScreen_ShowEntryOnly` shows the page WITHOUT setting seen and caught — reading a record is not meeting a thing.* ***Five things the work found that the ticket had not***: **(a) the start menu's DESCRIPTIONS were gated on HELP mode**, *so LR silently lost our own writing;* **(b) the first save migration sat on a callback the CONTINUE path does not take**, *so every existing save kept dead buttons;* **(c) R = AGAIN had become DEBUG-ONLY by accident** — *its include, its string and its script each landed inside a `#if DAEMONS_DEBUG` block and the two RELEASE ROMs would not compile, found by building all four rather than the one being tested;* **(d) `CB2_SetUpReshowBattleScreenAfterMenu` only clears a bag flag despite its name**, *so setting it as the main callback is a callback that does nothing — a black screen for ever; the party menu's `ReshowBattleScreenAfterMenu` is the real one;* **(e) the debug ENCOUNTER row now reads `163 POLL`**, *and its own promise of "L and R step by ten" works for the first time since it was written.* ***Still open, deliberately***: **`R` held in battle as PERSPECTIVE** (*9.2*) — *a second battle layout and a rule about what it costs, which is a decision rather than a convenience.*
issues.subject: T-179 L and R do nothing, and the game has uses for them

issues.description: ~~**28 of 75 portrait sources are drawn SMALLER than the sprite they become** (*found redrawing T-177's five, 2026-09-20, by `tools/prephires.py` reporting the figure's own drawn size*). ***The arithmetic nobody had done***: **the checkpoint draws on a fixed 8px grid, so a 512 canvas gives 64 ART PIXELS and the figure lands in about 50 of them** — *`sf_beauty.png` is 24x50, `sf_gamer.png` 24x49* — **which is then UPSCALED into a 64x64 sprite.** *The portraits that read are the hand drafts, whose figures are 270-290px and get DOWNSCALED: `portrait_juggler.png` is 161x289, `crush_girl` 292.* ***Downscaling averages, upscaling invents***, **and that is why T-177's outline improved every portrait but could not rescue BEAUTY's horns: they are two pixels in the source.** ***This is also a better measure than any T-177 tried*** (*AUC 0.80 against the same eye list, and unlike the others it names a cause that can be acted on*) — **and it is a property of the SOURCE, which is why measuring the built sprite could not find it.** ***The fix is the canvas***: **1024 gives 128 art pixels, so the figure is drawn at about twice the sprite and reduced into it** (*T-131 measured the cost at 82-106s a view against 23s at 512, which for a portrait is nothing*). ***Batch 1, the five T-177 named***: **BEAUTY, GAMER, POKEMON RANGER M and F, JUGGLER.** ***Then the rest of the 28, judged one at a time***: *a source at 50px is not automatically bad — SWIMMER F, YOUNGSTER and LEADER KOGA read perfectly well — so each is redrawn only where the redraw beats what is there, as T-169 kept 32 of 61.* ***Closes when*** *every portrait a player faces is drawn at or above the size it is shown at, or kept with a reason.*~~ — ***DONE AND CLOSED 2026-09-20*** (engine `5a7a8bd`, and the two batches after it; `gfx/drafts/t178/`): **14 of the 28 redrawn at 1024 and taken, 14 kept on purpose.** ***Taken***: *BEAUTY, JUGGLER, GAMER, RANGER M, RANGER F, CAMPER, CHANNELER, COOL TRAINER F, PICNICKER, COOL TRAINER M, STAFF SLATE, BURGLAR, PSYCHIC F, STAFF DOLDRUM SWIMMER, and TRELLIS (leader_erika).* ***Kept***: **BUG CATCHER, SAILOR, CUE BALL, ROCKET GRUNT M, STAFF CALLOW, STAFF BRAZEN, TAMER, LEADER BLAINE, SWIMMER F, SWIMMER M, YOUNGSTER, ELITE FOUR BRUNO, LEADER KOGA, STAFF DOLDRUM PICNICKER.** ***The rule the ticket was filed on held***: *a source drawn small is a reason to LOOK, not a reason to redraw — the last batch of eight produced exactly ONE take, because those were the ones that already read.* ***WHAT THE MODEL GETS WRONG, and this is worth more than the redraws***: **it drifts SPECIES** — *batch 1 drew a FOX for the jackal and both martens (and the fox is the CLEARS' animal), batch 3 drew a RODENT for the hyena and a FROG for the salamander, which would have put KOGA's species on a second leader* — **and it DROPS CLOTHES**, *returning a plain seagull in a cap and a plain penguin with no suit, where the suit is the joke.* **Both are standing negatives now, and a species is described by its FEATURES rather than named**: *the jackal's black-and-silver saddle and black-tipped tail, the marten's low body and cream throat bib, the bowerbird's short stout beak.* ***Three kept for reasons that are not about resolution at all***: **BRUNO's redraw put him in BLACK BELT's own gi** (*they are both kangaroos; the clothes are what separate them*), **STAFF BRAZEN's put a tarsier in a top hat**, *and CUE BALL's was crisper but bright cartoon green on a class whose whole read is a tough one.* ***The canvas rule is in 9.4*** (*v11.225*): **draw it at twice the size it is shown** — *1024 gives 128 art pixels where 512 gives 64, and the figure lands in about fifty of them.* ***And the check is in the tools***: *`prephires.py` reports a source's own drawn size, which is how the 28 were found.*
issues.subject: T-178 28 of 75 portrait sources are drawn SMALLER than the sprite they become

issues.description: ~~**Do any portraits need the cleaning pass, and what measures it?** (*raised by T-174's `style_compare.png`, 2026-09-20*). **Cut at 64x64, some portraits visibly come apart** — *`sf_beauty`'s hands and `sf_camper`'s fingers dissolve, and the aroma lady and the ruin maniac are worse* — **and `cleandraft.py` exists and was never run over the T-169 set.** ***But the premise it was raised on is already withdrawn***: *T-174 guessed the spriteforge portraits were the speckly ones and the measure said no —* **lone pixels 28.0% against 33.0%, loose fragments 0.2 against 0.4, over all 75** — *so a sweep by SOURCE would clean the wrong half.* ***The first job is therefore the MEASURE, not the cleaning***: **find the statistic that agrees with the eye on BEAUTY and CAMPER** — *candidates: thin-structure loss (a limb narrower than two pixels), outline continuity, or the share of the figure's colours used under 1% — and prove it by ranking the set and looking at the top and bottom five.* ***Then clean only what it names***, *and only where cleaning beats the drawing, as T-174 measured rather than assumed.* ***Closes when*** *a measure exists in `tools/`, it has been run over every portrait, and each portrait it names is either cleaned or kept with a reason.*~~ — ***DONE AND CLOSED 2026-09-20*** (engine `6eeb8e3c2`; `tools/gbaoutline.py`, and the same pass inside `gbachar.index`): **the ticket's first job was the MEASURE, and the measure's answer was NO.** ***Nine statistics against a list of broken portraits made by eye over all 72 that are ours***: *crumbs (share of the figure in same-colour blobs of 1-3 px), same-colour blobs per 100 px, colour churn, rare colours, thin structures, fringe, loose pieces, edge colours, outline share.* ***What they actually found***: **crumbs and churn rank a TWEED JACKET and a JUDO GI worst** — *they measure texture, not breakage* — **and loose pieces finds the portraits with TWO FIGURES in them** (*TWINS, SIS AND BRO, COOL COUPLE*). *The best reached AUC 0.93 and still named clean pictures at its extreme, so as a list of files to clean it would have cleaned the wrong half — which is exactly what this ticket was filed to avoid.* ***The honest reading***: **the eye was judging whether the SUBJECT is legible, and that is not a property of the pixels taken one at a time.** ***But the work found the CAUSE, which is better than a ranking.*** **The pictures that read draw 65-74% of their silhouette edge in their four darkest colours and never the bright ones; the ones that do not draw their edge in EVERY colour they have** — *100% of the palette, on seven of the nine.* **A drawing resized with LANCZOS has a blended edge, and a fifteen-colour adaptive fit spends its slots on that blend**: *BEAUTY holds five near-identical blues from one dress and has none left for her horns or her hands.* ***The quantizer cannot draw an outline, because an outline is a decision about what matters and it is only counting.*** ***So the fix is not cleaning files*** (`cleandraft.py` was never run): **every silhouette pixel takes the darkest colour its own picture already uses.** *Nothing added to a palette, no colour invented.* ***84 pictures, all of them ours***: **the 72 trainer portraits, the four hearsay portraits, the four intro pictures and the four back pics** — *the user's call was all of them, including the intro, where the white lab coats had no edge at all against a light background.* **Edge-in-its-darkest-four, averaged: 38% → 100%, and running it again redraws nothing.** *A back pic is a STRIP of 64x64 frames, so each frame is outlined on its own — outlining the strip whole would read one frame's feet against the next frame's head as silhouette.* ***Excluded on measurement rather than taste***: **the overworld**, *where an outline at 16x32 is most of the sprite (T-170).* ***What an outline cannot do***: **BEAUTY is improved and still fragmented** — *her horns and hands were lost in the drawing, not at the edge, and she is a REDRAW rather than a repair.*
issues.subject: T-177 Do any portraits need the cleaning pass, and what measures it?

issues.description: ~~**The first characters a player meets are the oldest art in the game** (*asked by the user 2026-09-20*). **Measured**: *the daemons are spriteforge (T-131) and 29 trainer portraits are (T-169) — but THIRTEEN `gbachar.py` jobs still build from `.jpeg` sources drafted through the older `daemon/sprite` pipeline*: **CRYSTAL's speech pic and her HEARSAY portrait, the PLAYER's two intro pics (LOGIC and INTUITION), AL's speech pic and his three battle pics, SCORN, HOLT, VERA, INIT and CAIRN** — *plus `gfx/intro/`'s nine MUSAI pieces and the title mark.* ***Why it matters***: **these are the FIRST things a player sees** — *the opening speech, your own character, the rival* — **and they are the only player-facing art that is neither spriteforge nor code.** *The user's reason is local-first and consistency of look, and T-169 measured the method that works: a RESTYLE from the existing drawing keeps identity (the animal, the clothes, the pose) where a prompt alone does not.* ***The job***: **a trial first, on CRYSTAL and the PLAYER, because they are the two most visible and the two hardest** — *64x96 at EIGHT bits per pixel with their own palette banks (engine.md's trap: the player's indices start at 65 and CRYSTAL's at 97; a wrong base is a screenful of confetti, not an error)* — **then the rest in batches, each judged AT THE SIZE THE GAME SHOWS IT, and kept where the current art wins, as T-169 kept 32 of 61.** ***Fixed***: *the fable holds (the Clears are foxes, AL is a fox — T-169 batch 6 caught that one as an otter), `gbachar.py` does the cut, and its JOBS name the file a batch may write.* ***TRIAL DONE 2026-09-20*** (`gfx/drafts/t174/`: `make.sh`, `src/`, `alt/`, `trial.png`; nothing written to the engine): **the method works, and the trial found the source that makes it work.** ***Restyle from the ROM PICTURE, not from the old `.jpeg`.*** *CRYSTAL restyled from her jpeg came back with a fresh backdrop and the framing collapsed — she cut small and off-centre. Restyled from `oak_speech/oak/pic.png` itself (the 64x96 the game shows, keyed to white and upscaled) she frames correctly and cuts clean at 0.45. The PLAYER's LOGIC pose cut clean from the jpeg-on-white at 0.4; INTUITION speckled.* ***And a trap of `gbachar.py`'s own, which its docstring predicted***: **its silhouette keying has a GREEN-HUE rule for vanilla's green backdrops, and our drafts carry green** — *so the rule ate the greens INSIDE the figures and both first cuts came back shredded, holes punched through coat and body. These three jobs need `hue=False`, which keys on the flat corners alone.* ***The recipe for the rest of the ticket***: *source = the in-ROM picture on white; denoise 0.4-0.45; `hue=False`; judge at 64x96, which is where the speckle shows.* **Nothing is written: the tool was reverted and the engine tree is clean.** ***SEEDS DRAWN 2026-09-20*** (`gfx/drafts/t174/seeds.png`, `intuition_round2.png`; still nothing written): **four seeds each at 0.45, and a second round for INTUITION at 0.35.** *CRYSTAL: seed 1917 is the one — calm muzzle, the coat stays white, the purple reads; 7 tints the coat lilac and 42 and 99 dissolve it. The PLAYER's LOGIC: all four hold hat, coat, strap and tail and make the face more simian, which is truer to the fable than the current near-human face; seed 7 is cleanest.* ***INTUITION does not restyle, and 0.35 did not rescue it***: **the coat thins at the hem and the walking leg blurs at every strength and every seed** — *the pose is the problem, not the knob: a walking figure is thin diagonal shapes, and 64 pixels cannot hold them, which is T-170's finding one size up.* ***REVERTED, AND THE EXPERIMENT THAT FOLLOWED, 2026-09-20***: **the user played it and called CRYSTAL and the player distorted; both are back to their drawings** (engine `49875fe36`). ***The user's diagnosis was right and the fault was mine***: *I fed the model the 64x96 ROM PICTURE upscaled — blocky input — so it invented detail. `gbachar.py` already downsamples with LANCZOS; the resolution had been thrown away before it got there.* ***The fix worked***: **the high-resolution drawing, its backdrop keyed by HUE** (*a flood fill could not clear it — the jpeg's green is not flat, which is why the first framing collapsed*), **padded to the ROM picture's own aspect (0.695 against 0.696) and drawn at 904px** — *`gfx/drafts/t174/crystal_hires.png`: the mush is gone at every strength.* ***But the style shift is not a strength knob***: **0.25, 0.30, 0.40 and 0.45 all produce the same picture** (*`crystal_strengths.png`*) — *the model restyles the face whatever it is asked, and CRYSTAL's broader muzzle and larger head are its idea of a fox, not noise.* ***So the ruling this experiment supports***: **the named cast keeps its drawings** — *spriteforge is for the 64px BATTLE art (the daemons, and the portraits where T-169 measured it winning four times in ten), and the intro cast is where the old drafts win.* ***What remains of T-174, if anything***: *HOLT, VERA, INIT, CAIRN, SCORN and AL's four are PORTRAITS, the same 64x64 surface T-169 worked on, so they could still be tried by the high-res recipe above — the intro three are decided.* ***TWO WRITTEN 2026-09-20*** (engine `e6c2d05d6`, the user's pick): **CRYSTAL is seed 1917 and the player's LOGIC pose is seed 7; INTUITION keeps its drawing.** *Both cut at 64x96 into their own palette banks -- CRYSTAL's indices 0-121 at base 97, the player's 0-95 at base 65, which is what vanilla's own files use; a wrong bank renders as confetti rather than an error (engine.md).* **The jobs now carry `hue=False` and a note saying why.** ***The user is testing it in play, and may revert to the fallback*** -- *keeping the old drawings for these three, which costs nothing but this commit.* ***So the split the ticket should expect***: **spriteforge for the standing pictures, the existing art kept where a pose defeats it** — *and the OVERWORLD is not an option for spriteforge at all (T-170 measured that), so the fallback for any character it cannot draw is the drawing already in the game.****Still open for the user***: *CRYSTAL's restyled face reads a little odd around the muzzle — the trial proves the pipeline, not that this particular draft ships.* ***Closes when*** *every player-facing character source is a spriteforge drawing or kept on purpose with a record.*~~ — ***DONE AND CLOSED 2026-09-20*** (`5a0facef`; `tools/prephires.py`, `gfx/drafts/t174/`: `batch.sh`, `batch2.sh`, `judge.py`, `judge.png`, `style_compare.png`, `FINDING.txt`): **the user's ruling is KEEP ALL NINE**, *which closes the ticket the way it said it would close — every player-facing character source is a spriteforge drawing or kept ON PURPOSE with a record.* ***The nine went three rounds***: **seeds 1917 and 7 at denoise 0.45, then one round at 0.32 with every observed failure named in the negative**, *each cut through `gbachar` and judged at the size the game shows it rather than at 904px — which is where the first attempt went wrong.* ***WHAT THE RESTYLE DOES TO THIS CAST, and three of the four are fixable***: **it SATURATES the fur** — *HOLT's brown otter comes back ORANGE at every seed and every strength, and orange is the CLEARS' colour, so an otter that reads as a fox breaks 9.4 where it is loudest;* **it DISSOLVES a light garment on light fur** — *AL's cream shirt returned as a BARE CHEST in three of his four poses;* **it DISSOLVES a small held object** — *CAIRN's slate and AL's monitor;* **and it loses a face's ONE MARK** — *INIT's dark muzzle, leaving a generic ginger dog.* ***Round 2 fixed the garment and the object at 0.32 with them named. Nothing fixed the fur.*** ***So the ruling rests on a comparison, not a preference***: **the art these nine already have is at least as clean as what comes back, and the restyle costs identity.** ***CAIRN was the single real candidate and was declined***: *its in-game tortoise is olive on olive and round 2 separates shell, shirt, apron and boots — but it buys that with a looser outline.* ***AND ONE CLAIM WITHDRAWN, WHICH IS WHY THE MEASURE WAS RUN***: **`style_compare.png` suggested the spriteforge portraits were the SPECKLY ones and the hand drafts the clean ones — three cells, an impression.** *Measured across all 75 portraits it does not hold:* **lone pixels 28.0% spriteforge against 33.0% hand-drafted, loose fragments 0.2 against 0.4, and the two worst on both measures are hand drafts.** *What is left is the narrow version above, and the general question went to* **T-177**. ***Also tidied***: **the `crystal` and `logic` jobs are back on the drawings the engine was reverted to** — *they had been left pointing at `sf_crystal.png`, which no longer existed, so a full `gbachar.py` run would have crashed on one and re-applied rejected art with the other.* *The rejected drafts are kept as `gfx/drafts/t174/sf_{crystal,logic}_rejected.png`, and `gbachar.main()` is guarded so `prephires.py` can import its keying.*

issues.description: ~~**The footprint in every Index entry is vanilla's** (*spotted by the user in play, 2026-09-20 — "some symbol or ink smudge" in the middle of the entry*). **It is the FOOTPRINT**: *Gen 3 prints a 16x16 1bpp mark between HT and WT, `graphics/pokemon/<species>/footprint.png`, and all 386 are still vanilla's paw prints.* ***Why it reads as a smudge***: **a paw print is a BODY** — *the one place in the Index where the fable's own rule is broken, on a screen whose every other line is a process.* ***The opportunity***: *a footprint is one bit per pixel and tiny, so it can be GENERATED — a mark derived from each daemon's own silhouette, or a per-type mark (the chart is the argument, and a type mark would say so).* ***Decide first***: **silhouette, type mark, or nothing at all** (*blanking it is legal: vanilla ships blanks for the unused slots*).~~ — ***DONE AND CLOSED 2026-09-20*** (engine `108b4b286`; `tools/genfootprints.py`): **the decision is the TYPE MARK**, *and the argument for it is what the entry page does not print* — **species, category, height and weight, and never the type**, *which Gen 3 keeps on the summary screen.* **So the slot carries the one fact the page lacks, and the chart is the argument** (invariant 3). ***The silhouette was the alternative and was ruled out on the format***: *sixteen pixels in ONE BIT is mush, and it would say nothing the picture beside it does not already say.* ***Eighteen marks, each its type's own 2.2 clause drawn flat***: **CONTENT** a token whole, **LOGIC** a turnstile, **VECTOR** an arrow, **CORRUPT** a blot spreading, **STRATUM** layers, **LEGACY** a cairn, **SWARM** many apart, **LATENT** a dashed box, **HARDENED** a plate, **ORACLE** a closed box that answers, **ENTROPY** a rising jag, **FLOW** a gradient descending, **GROWTH** a sprout, **SIGNAL** a carrier, **CONTEXT** two brackets framing, **FROZEN** a crystal, **EMERGENT** a spiral, **OPAQUE** filled solid. ***386 footprints written from `species_info.h`***, *so a retype changes the mark and the two cannot drift.* ***Verified in the ROM rather than by eye***: **eighteen distinct 32-byte blobs across every built footprint, so no vanilla paw survives**, *and all four ROMs exit 0.* ***One trap the tool hit and now documents***: **`[SPECIES_NONE] = {0},` is written on ONE LINE**, *so a non-greedy braced-block match runs straight through it and swallows BULBASAUR's entry with it* — **the parser splits on the label instead.** ***And one mark is carried by nobody***: **ORACLE** — *no daemon holds MYSTERY first, so the chart is complete and the bestiary is not.*
issues.subject: T-175 The footprint in every Index entry is vanilla's

issues.description: ~~**43 daemons a player can MEET still wear vanilla's front** (*measured 2026-09-20 after the user spotted MUTEX*). **T-131 drew 169 and these were missed** — *the meetable set it worked from came from wild encounters and scripts, and these arrive by EVOLUTION, gift or legendary*: **MUTEX, SIGKILL, MONOLITH, SUBSTRATE, OVERLAY, FORGE, DRUM, PUNCHCARD, MAGTAPE, MAINFRAME, BLOCKING, TRUST, HOPE, MOOD, ELATION, ABANDON, WITHDRAWAL, OBSESSION, CRAVING, ATTACHMENT, CLINGING, BROODING, CAPRICE, CUNNING, PRESCIENCE, TORPOR, BUOYANCY, GATHERING, LOOKOUT, ENTRAPMENT, RELEASE, BUILDUP, GOLDSET, HEARTBEAT, OUTLIER, ENGRAM, EDGECASE, TRIPLECORE, CIRCULAR, ORPHEUS, PROMETHEUS, ASCLEPIUS, PROTEUS* — *and the last four are the LEGENDARIES, which a player meets once and remembers.* ***The list is the measure***: *a daemon is in it if a script, a wild table, a trainer party or an EVOLUTION of any of those reaches it, and its `front.png` is byte-identical to upstream's.* **Batches as T-131 ran them**, *with the same recipe and contact sheets.* ***BATCH 1 DONE 2026-09-20*** (engine `660df59a2`; `gfx/drafts/t176/`: `make.sh`, `second.sh`, `fix.py`, `PICKS.txt`, `sheet.png`, `second.png`): **nine taken — MUTEX, MONOLITH, FORGE, DRUM, MAGTAPE, MAINFRAME, BLOCKING, EDGECASE, TRIPLECORE** — *front, back and icon each, since all three were vanilla for every one of them. Sprites 44% to 47%, every sprite past half at 50.6%.* ***Three held, and the reason is the same one***: **PUNCHCARD, SUBSTRATE and OUTLIER are CONCEPTS rather than creatures** — *a punched card, a thing with mass, one mark that sets it apart* — *and the model drew a lizard, a robot and a symmetrical blob; a second round with sharper prompts got SUBSTRATE's front and nothing else.* **They are the case for drawing in code, as T-167 drew its objects: a card with real holes is trivial to author, and so is one dark patch over one eye.* ***BATCH 2 DONE 2026-09-20*** (engine `8694b4cce`; `gfx/drafts/t176/batch2.sh`, `batch2b.sh`, `sheet2.png`, `second2.png`): **eleven taken — TRUST, HOPE, MOOD, ELATION, LOOKOUT, CUNNING, TORPOR, PRESCIENCE, ENTRAPMENT, GATHERING, BUILDUP** — *the egg a player is handed, the water daemons, the early island grass. Daemon fronts 47% to 49%; every sprite 52.8%.* ***The recipe's edge, now measured twice***: **a CONCRETE clause lands and an ABSTRACT one does not.** *TRUST's "still half inside a cracked shell" drew itself; LOOKOUT's "long enough to see over everything" drew a stick figure until it was asked for a ferret standing upright, and MOOD's "floats at whatever level the water is" drew a blob until it was asked for a round mouse with a ball-tipped tail.* ***THE FOUR CONCEPTS DRAWN IN CODE 2026-09-20*** (engine `d9fad938a`; `tools/gendaemons.py`): **PUNCHCARD, SUBSTRATE, OUTLIER and RELEASE** — *a card with rows of real holes and two cutting blades; three stacked slabs with blunt legs, which is a thing that HAS a mass; a plain round creature with ONE longer ear and one dark patch, which is the whole of what an outlier is; and a tail lamp that stays attached because it is drawn attached.* **The tool takes the greys and the four STREAK MARKERS from `gbasprite.py` itself**, *so the drawings ramp into each daemon's type colour like every other.* ***Daemon fronts past half at 51%; every sprite 53.7%.*** ***BATCH 3 DONE 2026-09-20*** (engine `604e0573d`; `batch3.sh`, `batch3b.sh`, `sheet3.png`, `second3.png`): **twelve, and the three LEGENDARIES among them** — *ORPHEUS crested and mid-song, PROMETHEUS carrying the brand in its talons (the object stayed attached, which is what the held four could not do), ASCLEPIUS jagged and alert, and SIGKILL, ENGRAM, WITHDRAWAL, OBSESSION, CRAVING, BROODING, CLINGING with them.* ***Two needed the concrete-shape rule applied twice***: **OVERLAY lost the SEAM between its layers until it was asked for armour plating with the older body showing at neck and legs**, *and CIRCULAR drew a spinning top with no creature in it until it was asked for a creature balanced upside down on its crest with its legs in a V.* ***One judgement worth recording***: **CLINGING keeps its rocks** — *its entry says it holds rocks, so they are the pose rather than scenery; OBSESSION's back was standing ON a rock and was swapped for its other seed.* ***Daemon fronts 54%, every sprite 56.1%.*** ***What this pair of batches established***: **the model draws a CREATURE from a concrete clause and fails on a CONCEPT** — *and the answer is not a better prompt, it is a different instrument: the code tools that drew T-167's objects draw these in an afternoon, and place every pixel on purpose.* ***RELEASE held***: *"all of it, at once, and then dark" — the tail lamp never lands; one seed drew a lamp POST standing beside it. It joins PUNCHCARD, SUBSTRATE and OUTLIER as candidates for code.* ***Two cleaning notes***: *FORGE's chosen back cleaned to 22x14 — the fill ate the chimney — so its other seed was used; and DRUM, MAGTAPE and MONOLITH sat on boxes that shade unevenly, which needed the BAND flood T-165 wrote rather than a tolerance around one seed.*~~ — ***BATCH 4, AND CLOSED 2026-09-20*** (engine `e3f702a9c`): **the last seven — GOLDSET, HEARTBEAT, PROTEUS, ABANDON, BUOYANCY, ATTACHMENT, CAPRICE.** *GOLDSET took a second round: every seed drew a small PERSON in a leaf skirt until the prompt forbade arms, legs and a face on a body — 9.4 rules the actors are animals and the daemons are not people either. Its pot was then removed in code, being a prop rather than the daemon.* — ***The measure that opened this ticket now returns ZERO***: **no daemon a player can meet — by wild table, script, trainer party, gift, evolution or legendary — still wears vanilla's front.** *43 redrawn across four batches; daemon fronts 44% to 55%, every sprite in the game 48.8% to 57.5%.* ***What the four batches taught, and it is reusable***: **the Index entry is the right prompt when it names a SHAPE and the wrong one when it names a CONDITION.** *TRUST's "half inside a cracked shell" drew itself; LOOKOUT's "long enough to see over everything" drew a stick figure until it was asked for a ferret standing upright. Four entries name no shape at all — PUNCHCARD, SUBSTRATE, OUTLIER, RELEASE — and those were drawn in CODE (`tools/gendaemons.py`), where a card can have real holes and a tail lamp stays attached because it is drawn attached.*

issues.description: ~~**An animation theatre in the debug build — any routine, played on demand**~~ — ***Done 2026-09-17*** (engine `a3106718b`; `tools/theatre.lua`; `docs/engine.md` §5 and trap 19). **In a debug battle, SELECT at "What will X do?" opens it: LEFT/RIGHT step one routine, UP/DOWN ten, A plays it between the two daemons on the field, START swaps sides, SELECT teaches it to that side's daemon and re-patches the streaks, B returns.** ***L and R were the first design and FireRed's HELP system took them*** — *trap 19.* **Capture: `tools/theatre.lua` runs inside mGBA's Scripting window and reads `.theatre/theatre.cmd` — `hold`, `wait`, `shot`, `burst` — so buttons are held for exact frames and every frame is saved as the GBA drew it** (*a key tapped into the window from outside reached the game about half the time*). ***Proved on screen the same day***: *RESTORE vanilla and draft, PERSPECTIVE and WRITE captured as filmstrips (`gfx/drafts/animations/t135_exemplars.png`), and **T-132's acceptance test passed**: a wild ROVERCUB taught TRICKLE, JITTER, PULSE and WRITE took exactly FLOW's light, ENTROPY's light and SIGNAL's DARK step (the light one vanishes on GROWTH) in battle, and the Index drew the same species with the blank grey (148,148,148).* **Not done: the release ROMs have no theatre, by design** (*`nm` finds no `DbgTheatre` in either*).

issues.description: ~~**The animation rule — what a routine's animation may show**~~ — ***Decided 2026-09-17: vision.md 9.24, v11.213***; *RESTORE released as its exemplar (engine `382bda0af`)*. (*T-134, wave 0; a decision to draft, not a job to start*). **Written as a 9.x section and approved before any family is touched**: *what an animation depicts (the process the routine names, not the creature's body doing something), where colour may appear (9.4 and PERSPECTIVE's precedent: colour where it means something, grey as the ground), whether a routine's own TYPE colour tints its effects, what the streaks do during an animation, and the budget — script-only (vanilla's effect sprites, re-sequenced and re-tinted) against new effect graphics.* ***Drafted on three exemplars before it is written as a rule***: **RESTORE, PERSPECTIVE (already ours) and one CONTENT attack** — *shown in the T-136 theatre, approved on screen.* ***Drafted and APPROVED 2026-09-17*** (*`gfx/drafts/animations/t135_exemplars.png`*): **the proposed rule** — *(1) an animation shows the PROCESS its routine names, never a creature exerting its body or gathering energy from outside; (2) the daemon's own palette is the medium, and grey is the ground: losing something is drawn as draining toward grey, getting it back as colour returning — which costs invariant 5 nothing (8.6); (3) the only colour an effect may add is a TYPE's — the routine's own, from `TYPE_COLOR` — never vanilla's decorative yellows, pinks and blue stars; (4) the streaks are part of the palette, so whatever happens to a daemon's colour happens to what it knows; (5) in Halftone the frame's greying wins (8.6a) and PERSPECTIVE's flash stays the one exception; (6) script first — re-sequencing and re-tinting vanilla's tasks and sprites — and a new effect graphic only when no existing one can mean the process (T-137).* ***The exemplars***: **RESTORE redrawn (debug ROMs only, `.if DAEMONS_DEBUG`): its colour drains to grey and returns in three ticked steps — a checkpoint reloading**; *PERSPECTIVE already obeys (1), (2) and (4)*; **WRITE (vanilla TACKLE) is the open one** — *a lunge and a shake is a body doing something, and under (1) and (3) a write would land on the target as a brief flash of the attacker's type colour rather than a shove; not built until the rule is approved.*
issues.subject: T-135 The animation rule — what a routine's animation may show

**wave 4 — the late types and COPY.** *Alongside: T-137 the 188 effect graphics, redrawn only as a family needs one, and T-138 the 112 renamed routines still describing vanilla's move.* ***The discrepancy is settled***: *vision.md v11.212 records RECOVER → RESTORE, and why.* ***The scale***: **354 of 356 animation scripts vanilla, 24 families.**~~ — ***Done 2026-09-18, every family released: `animcensus.py` reports 0 of 356 vanilla (vision.md 9.24, v11.217). Seen in the game: SHELL in Doldrum, in FLOW blue, beside a local who kept her colours.* ***Cosmetic, left***: *a daemon that reflects in water shows its slot's generic reflection palette.* **T-164 is unblocked.**

*sheets approved the same day; all twenty-six views decode at 64×64 and are in all four ROMs with their palettes; `streaks.h` flags 168; daemon fronts 169 of 386*) ***EVERY DAEMON A PLAYER CAN MEET IS REDRAWN*** — **batches 1–15, 168 species with streaks, from the first route through the League and THE MARGINS.** *Left under this ticket: MISSINGNO (T-163), the backs that face forward (T-166, twenty-five), the twenty-five overworld objects (T-133), and the species the player can never meet, which keep vanilla's art by the scope written above.*: **THE MARGINS end — VIGILANCE, RUMINATE, PERIPHERY, COMFORT, GRASP, HOARDING, ILLUSION, IMITATION, STARTLE, INSTINCT, CALLOUS, REPAY, ARMOURING.** *ILLUSION took the most work: seed 42's back lost its head and antlers to the fill, seed 1917 was drawn inside a picture frame that `keep_largest` kept (the frame IS the largest shape), and the dark redraw is side-on — on T-166's list.
