LEMMA MIND's space is an underscore in its file name (`GBA_NAME` in `gbasprite.py`); the game's name is unchanged. MULTICAST's dark box sat inside a pale strip no corner fill could reach, so it is cleared by colour and then everything but the bat itself.*: **PIPELINE, FERRY, SLURP, VICE, DRAGNET, COLDVAULT, TRACKER, WIRETAP, HAUNTPROC, COLDREAD, RESENTMENT, FOSSILNET** — *Victory Road, the League and the champion's teams; LEMMA MIND held for batch 13 because its name has a space the art pipeline's file names do not handle yet.* ***COLDREAD is a snowy owl***: *its first drafts drew a pale human woman, too near vanilla's caricature for this slot, and were replaced — the owl states what you are about to say.* *PIPELINE, WIRETAP and HAUNTPROC redrawn dark after losing pale bodies to the fill; FERRY's and TRACKER's boxes removed; four coloured drafts greyed after cleaning.*: **CRYOGEN, DYNAMO, SHELL, FLICKER, WILDFIRE, CONJECTURE, AXIOMKICK, REBUTTAL, OVERDRIVE, SCHEDULER, GUARDIAN**, *all from words, the end of the Fuchsia-to-Cinnabar roster.* *SHELL first drew a bare seashell and AXIOMKICK and REBUTTAL drew people; all three redrawn with people and armour negative. SCHEDULER still reads as an armoured ogre.* ***MISSINGNO left out on purpose***: *it stands in an old Unown slot at level 80, and what a glitch daemon looks like is a design question, not a redraw — for the user.*: **QUORUM, CHILLER, JETSTREAM, SMOGSTACK, TRANCE, BREAKER, THEOREM, MIME, LANDFILL, LIVELOCK, CAIRNLING, HANDLER**, *all from words, Fuchsia to Cinnabar.* *HANDLER's first ducks lost their white heads to the fill and were redrawn dark; its thin legs still sample as one solid block — flagged as the weakest of the batch. MIME reads as a human clown and THEOREM as a bodybuilder, as PROOF did. MIME, HANDLER and JETSTREAM greyed after cleaning; CAIRNLING's seed 42 drew a skeleton warrior.*: **the story's own — CANON, MANIFOLD, ROVERBYTE, MUSAI, CAREMUSAI, CODEMUSAI, SEEKMUSAI, ARTSAI, STARR, from their concepts — and PREDICTOR, THREAD, SPYWARE from words.** ***A correction***: *batch 6's note said `gfx/front/` had no concept left undrawn; nine were, because the check compared filenames and these nine had never been built. Found building batch 9's roster.* *STARR's concept redraw was brown and greyed after cleaning (`fix.py`); two hand-placed streak boxes. SMOGSTACK, TRANCE, LANDFILL, QUORUM, CHILLER, JETSTREAM and the rest from Fuchsia to Cinnabar are batch 10.*: **TARPIT, BADSEED, ENSEMBLE, KEEPER, SEEDLING, UPSTREAM, REAPER, UPTIME, MOCK, ROOTKIT, EMERGENCE, STAMPEDE**, *all from words — Celadon's last four and Fuchsia and the Safari Zone; PREDICTOR, THREAD, SPYWARE, TRANCE, LANDFILL and SMOGSTACK start batch 9.* ***"Small in the frame" is now in every prompt, and it worked***: *all twenty-four views cleaned with no hand-placed streak box, the first batch to.* *BADSEED and ENSEMBLE first drew potted flowers and headless palm trees and were redrawn with pots and trees negative; ENSEMBLE still has one head, not several. Five coloured drafts cleaned in colour and greyed after; REAPER's enclosed background cleared by colour.*: **WISP, DUALCORE, REVENANT, BOOTSTRAP, BLIGHT, HONEYPOT, OUTBREAK, PARTITION, RAMROD, MITE, TRACER, SPAGHETTI**, *all from words — Lavender and Halftone Tower, Routes 7, 8, 12 and 16, Celadon's benchmark and the hideout; TARPIT, BADSEED, ENSEMBLE and KEEPER start batch 8.* ***A new failure, and its fix***: **a draft that fills the frame with a pale body loses the body to the background fill** (*DUALCORE's first pairs, BLIGHT's first picks*); **redrawn "small in the frame" and dark it survives**, *and a coloured draft whose pale parts would match the background once greyed is now cleaned IN COLOUR and greyed after, every pixel but the streak markers (batch 7's `fix.py`).* *The model will not draw one body with two heads, so DUALCORE is two birds side by side — which is its Index entry's "Two of them".*: **INDEXER, INJECTOR, BROADCAST, FLOOD, HIBERNATE from their concepts — the last five in `gfx/front/`, finishing the lines batches 1–2 began — and TAPPOINT, SENTRY, HOTPATH, INFERENCE, LATENCY, STACK, RELIC from words** (*Vermilion to Rock Tunnel and Diglett's Cave; MITE and BLIGHT are batch 7*). *RELIC's first backs drew a skeleton warrior and were redrawn as a mouse from behind; TAPPOINT's square had a darker rim, so `fix.py` gains `unrim` and `despeck`.*: **RELAY, OVERFLOW, SURGE, RUBRIC, LOCUS, ROVERSEER from their concepts (as batch 1), and CAPSULE, PROOF, LULL, SPINLOCK, COOKIE from words** — *the rest of the Doldrum area, Vermilion's benchmark lead and the rival's first evolutions; SENTRY, HOTPATH, INFERENCE, MITE and BLIGHT are batch 6.* *`fix.py` gains `unshadow` for a drop shadow touching the feet (LULL), which the background fill cannot reach.*: **the Mt. Moon Super Nerds' four and the Doldrum routes and BASIN — SENTINEL, FUSE, SLUDGE, FUMES, HUNCH, SNARE, WEED, SPAWN, LOOP, BEACON, PULSAR**, *eleven from words; CAPSULE, RELAY, PROOF, LULL and SPINLOCK are batch 5.* *Six views desaturated before cleaning, two hand-placed streak boxes, and LOOP's front drawn on a dark square (`fix.py`) — whose automatic strokes had landed on the square, so a box drawn on a square now gets its streaks placed by hand too.*: **Mt. Moon and Route 4 — ECHO, ANOMALY, PAYLOAD, FAULT, ESCALATE, NOZZLE, PINCER, STUB, DRIFTNET**, *all nine from words (none had a concept), two seeds per view up front, which took one pass where batch 2 took three.* ***Two rules the batch made standard***: **a draft drawn with colour in its BODY is desaturated before cleaning** (*PAYLOAD's green caps, DRIFTNET's blue dome, and the four swimmers drawn pale blue, which `gbasprite.py`'s accent shift turned GOLD on a FLOW body*); **and a pale body can be emptied by the background fill** (*FAULT's first back became an outline, and was redrawn darker*). *Four views take hand-placed streak boxes (`PICKS.txt`).*~~ — ***DONE AND CLOSED 2026-09-20*** (engine `98b52f1f8`, docs `e4b55191`; `tools/gbareach.py`, `gfx/drafts/t131/`, `gfx/drafts/t131_twelve.py`): **the ticket's own measure now returns ONE, and the one is the EGG PICTURE.** ***What closed it was replacing the estimate with a tool.*** **This ticket was scoped at *'about 190-200 species a player can meet or evolve into'* — and T-176 then found 43 it had missed.** *An estimate cannot be re-checked, so `gbareach.py` reads the game instead*: **wild tables, every trainer party, every script, the trades, the starters, and the transitive closure of `evolution.h` over all of them.** *213 species are reachable.* ***It found TWELVE that had never been converted at all*** — **vanilla art AND vanilla names, absent from the 229-name register**: *the ten Johto strays vanilla sprinkles into the SEVII trainer parties, met by anyone who plays past the Elite Four, and LUGIA and HO-OH at Navel Rock.* **The register was not wrong; the list it was checked against came from the mainland.** ***All twelve converted together*** — **name, Index category and entry in both editions, bucketed in the register, then the art**: *POLL → SUPERVISOR, PILOT → SOUNDING, STARVED → QUOTA, FAKEROOT, DUPLEX, WARNING, CACHE, and TRITON and PHOENIX into MYTH.* ***DUPLEX is drawn in CODE***: **three rounds and eight seeds returned a single-headed quadruped or two separate animals** — *the DUALCORE wall from batch 7, and this entry does not allow DUALCORE's answer, because 'from opposite ends' IS the daemon.* ***Four cleaning faults, each now a tool in `gfx/drafts/t131/fix.py`***: **a grey FRAME round a near-white interior** (*the flood takes the frame and stops; flooding 'anything light' instead eats a pale creature — `deframe` floods in layers at 512, where the outline has no gaps*); **a pale creature on a pale ground is the wrong problem for a flood at all** (*`by_outline` takes the largest dark-bordered shape, holes filled*); **the key must not be a colour in the art** (*keyed blue, TRITON's blue-grey dragon fell inside cleandraft's own tolerance and the flood ate the animal, leaving 151 loose pixels*); **and the strip it was drawn standing on touches the feet**, *so nothing else can remove it — `unground` knows it by shape.* ***Two views defeated the streak placement outright*** (*SOUNDING's torso is a thin diagonal, TRITON's body is mostly wing*): **`place_streaks` chooses the band from the MASK and shortens the stroke until four fit on real body.** ***Census***: **daemon fronts 55% → 59%, every sprite in the game 57.5% → 59.9%.** ***Deliberately NOT in scope***: *the 159 species no map, party, script or evolution reaches — this ticket said from the start that everything past the cut-off keeps vanilla's, and `gbareach.py` is what makes that claim checkable rather than asserted.*

issues.description: ~~**Two Index entries were never written: WORM and MIME**~~ — ***Done 2026-09-17*** (engine `a6e482ff9`) (*found 2026-09-17 by T-47's read*). **Both are vanilla prose in both editions, and the Game Boy source never wrote them either** — *so the port carried nothing, and nobody noticed because each had been touched once.* **WORM** (*Ekans slot, `PROPAGATE`, on Route 4*) *is vanilla's LeafGreen line with `port_names.py`'s substitution run through it — "Eats the eggs of birds, such as PACKET and PING, whole", with no full stop* — **in BOTH editions, so FireRed shows LeafGreen's vanilla.** **MIME** (*Mr. Mime slot, `IMITATIVE`, MATTE's lead*) *is vanilla word for word in FireRed — "adept at conning people" — and vanilla with a move renamed in LeafGreen, "will suddenly REPEAT the offender".* **Both are GAMUT species, so each wants machinery as its subject and the mind left unsaid, CONTENT saying what it is and CONTEXT what somebody made of it, as SUBSTRATE's pair does.** *New Index prose is writing and wants its wording approved before it goes in* ***Written, with the wording approved first***: **WORM** — *CONTENT "It copies itself into anything that will run it, and leaves from there. It does not need to be carried. It does not stop." CONTEXT "Nobody sent it. Everyone who received it passed it on. It is counted by where it has been, and it has been everywhere."* **MIME** — *CONTENT "It mimes a wall with its hands, and things stop at the wall. There is no wall. Nothing that stopped has checked." CONTEXT "It copies what blocks the way, down to how the hands are held. Everything that meets the copy treats it as the thing."* ***A character count is not a width***: **at forty-two characters MIME's CONTEXT line measured 239px against the 234px Index line vanilla demonstrates, and at that width the approved wording needed four lines** — *so the text is wrapped by pixels, and one word was trimmed ("whatever" → "what"), with approval.* **The widest Index line is 234px in both editions; each text is in its own edition's two ROMs and not the other's, and the vanilla lines are gone from all four.** *The Game Boy build is a reference and not updated further, so its `dex_text.asm` keeps vanilla's.*
issues.subject: T-130 Two Index entries were never written: WORM and MIME

issues.description: ~~**The player's reflection in water is vanilla's colours**~~ — ***Done 2026-09-17*** (`tools/genreflection.py`; engine `4ddf96d79`) (*found 2026-09-17 by the title-strike sweep: T-52 recorded it as "still open" on 2026-09-14 and nothing picked it up*). **`graphics/object_events/palettes/player_reflection.pal` is byte-identical to `upstream/master`** *while `player.pal` — the figure you walk as — is ours*, **so on any reflective tile the figure beneath you is drawn in the old colours.** *T-52 notes the surf body moved onto the BOX's greys, which the reflection should follow too.* **Derive the reflection from `player.pal` the way vanilla derives its own (a darkened, blued copy of the same sixteen), rather than typing a second palette, and check it on a reflective map in both editions** ***The reflection is DERIVED, by a rule fitted to vanilla's own five palette/reflection pairs***: **every colour kept at 75% and lifted by (89, 98, 90).** ***The model with the best score was the wrong one***: *a nearest-colour rule predicted vanilla's held-out colours best (11.5 of 255 against 15.4), but on OUR palette it turned the near-black brown, the tan mint and the cream icy cyan — hue drift averaging 32° and reaching 137°. Its error was measured on vanilla's saturated colours, and this figure is greys and browns, whose nearest saturated neighbours lend them their hue.* **The one-tint mix cannot turn a grey into a colour, drifts 6°, and scores the same as a line.** *The tool finds stale reflections itself — a base that differs from upstream with a reflection that does not — so a palette redrawn later cannot quietly repeat this; `player.pal` was the only one.*
issues.subject: T-129 The player's reflection in water is vanilla's colours

issues.description: ~~**The town interiors are vanilla's**~~ (*asked 2026-09-16: "adjust all overworld and buildings sprites that remain"; scoped "interiors only, skip hoenn_building"*). ***Buildings are TILESETS, not sprites***: 21 still-vanilla secondary tilesets over 109 layout-slots, and **the interiors are not wholly vanilla today** — `gTileset_Building` is the primary for 184 layouts and is already ours, so what is vanilla is the per-building-type overlay. *Measured properly, that overlay is most of what you see: **21,287 of 29,601 cells (72%)** draw from the vanilla secondary, and per building it runs 99.9% (pokemon_tower), 98.8% (cable_club), 96.2% (condominiums) down to 6.1% (generic_building_1, effectively free to skip).* ***`pokemon_tower` IS OUT OF SCOPE AND MUST STAY OUT***: **8.6a is "decided and built 2026-09-13" — Halftone is grey, all seven floors, tiles and people** — *and `fieldmap.c:843-884` ships `DaemonsIsHalftone()` / `DaemonsGreyHalftoneFrame()` to do it once a frame, so colour drawn there is erased every frame.* ***The scripted-id hazard is narrow and known***: only `PokemonLeague` (9 names, 20 refs), `GameCorner` (9/12), `TrainerTower` (4/4) and `DepartmentStore` (1/1) carry `METATILE_` labels — `metatile_labels.h` is hand-maintained, so these are literal addresses — **and `CeladonCity_GameCorner/scripts.inc` rewrites five cells to open the hideout stair (`0x29D 0x29E 0x29F 0x2A6 0x2A7`, shut `0x292`/`0x2CF`) while `cable_club.inc` reaches into `METATILE_GameCorner_*` from another map entirely.** ***VERDIGRIS FIRST, from a concept approved 2026-09-16***: *the frame, in commerce* — **bronze where the building asserts itself, verdigris ONLY where hands and time reach, green only on what is alive** — *the store is the thing that went up (craft rule 2's kid outside is right), the hideout is an office under a floor Corpus already owns (the sign reads CORPUS GAME CORNER), and the hotel keeps no daemon fixture because it is "a hotel for people".* ***Done 2026-09-16 — FOUR of the five buildings, 13 rooms, 0 collision changes across every one of them***: `gTileset_VerdigrisTable` *(the restaurant and hotel, 40 blocks / 105 tiles)*, `_VerdigrisStore` *(six floors, 57 / 100)*, `_VerdigrisBlock` *(four floors, 41 / 72)* and `_VerdigrisFloor` *(three rooms, 47 / 86, with all nine script-pinned ids reserved so the hideout stair still opens)*. ***It took three drafts and each failure was specific***: *(1) classifying `behaviour == 0` as wall swallowed every table, machine bank and the school's long table — **wall is what a border flood-fill reaches through blocked, ROLE-LESS cells**, and 98 distinct vanilla blocks came back as 5; (2) drawing per cell rather than per **cluster** — a kitchen is one 5×7 block holding a counter, a stove, a dresser and a plate; (3) structure without **surface** — vanilla spends 16–25% of every floor cell on its pattern and the draft spent 0.8%, so 57% of the room was one flat colour.* **Fixed by deriving rather than inventing**: *fixtures from the game's own metatile behaviours (128 counter, 130 shelf, 157 window…), wall kinds from what vanilla drew there (**27 hotel wall ids collapse to five kinds** by colour signature), and the two rooms given separate grounds because vanilla does — commonest colour 56.8% → 23.5%.* ***And a chair landed on an NPC***: *drawing chairs on open floor put one under a T-119 local at (1,2); `_map_events()` now derives every warp/object/sign cell from each map.json's own `layout` field, since the layout id does not name its map and mangling only works by luck.* ***The second batch taught three more, and all three were the same mistake — a derived rule applied too bluntly***: *(1) **a window is an OPENING, not a colour** — the classifier keys on blue, so the Game Corner's sky band and the whole store roof came out a field of panes; when windows are more than a third of a room's wall they are not windows, and they are demoted to whatever that room's wall is otherwise made of (it fired on exactly three rooms — roof 47.8%, Game Corner 47.9%, prize room 43.5% — and left the condominiums' real windows at 12–18% alone); (2) **"dark" is the surround vanilla leaves OUTSIDE a room, never a wall material** — letting it win the demotion vote turned that sky band into black slabs; (3) **each trade needs its own GROUND** — a third warm neutral made the condominiums look unfinished, and cool stone against the store's parquet and the hotel's carpet is what made them read as three buildings.* **And two grounds needed their own pattern rather than `_weave`: the Game Corner is a CHEQUER (a grid you stand inside) and the landings are TILED (grout on an 8px grid).** *One misdiagnosis corrected on the way: the black bars down the condominiums' landings are vanilla's own, not a bug of ours.* ***THE SCHOOL IS SPLIT PER TOWN, decided 2026-09-16, and that closes this ticket***: **one tileset served two rooms in two towns doing two different things** — *`VIRIDIAN_CITY_SCHOOL` is **CALLOW's** classroom and `CELADON_CITY_CONDOMINIUMS_ROOF_ROOM` is **VERDIGRIS's** lecture room, which is not a classroom at all: it reads you a DAEMON Lecture and hands over a MUSAI.* **Their plans are all but identical** (*windows at (1,1), a region map at (7,1), bookshelves at (8,2), a long table at (4,4), the mat at (4,7); the lecture room adds a lectern at (7,3)*), **so the split is about TOWN and FUNCTION, not layout** — *a tileset apiece, as `checkpoint_indigo` already serves exactly one layout.* ***CALLOW's classroom is built of its own BENCHMARK's materials***: **poured concrete under a surveyor's grid (T-113), so THE GRID ON THE BOARD IS THE GRID UNDER YOUR FEET** — *the type table drawn as a lattice of identical chalk cells, the desks facing it, and the one living thing in the room a plant on the sill grown past its cane, which nobody remarks on.* **The room's own shipped text was already the lesson**: *"I have to have the table by Friday. I do not have to understand it. I have to have it." / "It is all on the board." / "Learn the table. It does not change."* ***VERDIGRIS's lecture room is built of the block it sits on top of*** — *cool stone landings, bronze fittings, verdigris only where a hand goes — and its board is a lecture board rather than a table to be learned.* **`gTileset_CallowSchool` 16 blocks / 43 tiles, `gTileset_VerdigrisLecture` 13 / 26, 0 collision changes in either, and `gTileset_School` now has ZERO consumers.** ***THE SCHOOL SPANS TWO TOWNS AND THAT IS OPEN***: *`VIRIDIAN_CITY_SCHOOL` is **CALLOW's** and `CELADON_CITY_CONDOMINIUMS_ROOF_ROOM` is Verdigris's — and the second is not a schoolroom but a **lecture room** (it hands out a MUSAI). The concept's sharpest paragraph was built on Callow's text.* **Split the tileset per town, defer it as a Callow ticket, or accept one shared instruction-room idiom — undecided**

issues.description: ~~**The three obstacles a field move clears are still vanilla's**~~ — ***Done 2026-09-16*** (`tools/genprops.py`): **`cut_tree` (55 objects), `rock_smash_rock` (97) and `strength_boulder` (58) — 210 objects on three 16×16 sheets, redrawn.** *They are not miscellaneous: they are the three things a field move removes, and the bible had already named all three moves — **CUT → PRUNE** ("the obstacle is literally a tree"), **ROCK SMASH → CRACK** ("you crack a rock and you crack a problem"), **STRENGTH → DISPLACE**.* ***The tree is the one that had to change***: **T-61 replaced vanilla's conifer across the General tileset with a round broadleaf and it is shipped — 204 of that tileset's 640 tiles differ from vanilla — and Route 2 loads `gTileset_General` and carries five cut-trees**, *so our broadleaves and vanilla's dark bush were on screen together.* **And our tree is the LIGHT one, which is the reverse of what the first draft assumed**: *measured off `broadleaf()`, LIT 38.5% + LEAF 36.8% against DARK 13.4% and DEEP 11.3%, where vanilla's `cut_tree` spends 52% of its ink on the darkest green.* `npc_green` *has no LIT, so both light bands collapse onto `l` and it becomes the BODY colour rather than a highlight; luminance lines the ramp up (l 178 / J 111 / N 54 against LEAF 169 / DARK 110 / DEEP 71).* ***The rocks go grey, and that is a judgment call with nothing in the bible ruling on it***: **`item_ball.png` — ours, 16×16, in the same `npc_white` slot — spends four colours and no dither, a hard `K` rim over flat `w`/`g`/`G` bands**, *which is also SLATE's vocabulary; vanilla's olive-and-sand dither reads as mossy earth.* **The rock is angular and fissured and the boulder smooth and round, so the two never read as one object** — *one is broken open, the other shoved aside.* **Reversible: revert this file's ROCK and BOULDER art and rerun.** ***THE FIRST "REDRAW" WAS A TRANSCRIPTION AND WAS DISCARDED***: **it came out 248 of 256 cells identical to vanilla — twelve of sixteen rows byte for byte** — *which is not a conversion, and would have put Nintendo-derived pixels into THIS repo as source literals, the one thing `CLAUDE.md` promises not to do.* **`gbatrees.py` and `gbaground.py` do derive from vanilla pixel by pixel, but they READ it out of `engineGba` at runtime; `gbacopyright.py` lifts vanilla's font and SAYS SO, with a reason.** *A tree has no such reason — its whole job is to stop matching vanilla.* **The shipped art is 15% / 7% / 9% identical to vanilla over INK cells.** ***Four wrong readings of one 16×16 sprite came first***, *each inferred from a projection and each refuted by the next measurement, until a connected-component pass answered it outright* — **engine.md trap 15 now carries the general form.** ***And the tool imports nothing that writes***: **`import gbatrees` RUNS it, and under `--write` its own flag reads `True` off the shared `sys.argv`, which would have rewritten the tileset** — *proved, not suspected; see trap 16.* **`strength_boulder` keeps NO conversion rule and must not be given one** — *every single-frame 16×16 misc sheet goes without, and one frame in raster order is already correct.*

issues.description: ~~**Four PAIR classes stand as two single sprites of the wrong animals**~~ — ***Done 2026-09-16*** (`tools/genpairs.py`; engine `5392c4812`) (*found by `tools/spritejoin.py` 2026-09-16, 28 objects*). **A pair class is ONE trainer standing as TWO map objects**, *so "one species per class" is the wrong question — the picture has to be the two animals those two sheets ALREADY are.* ***T-126 settled the method on `COOL_COUPLE`***: **its two ibexes became a wolf and a falcon, because a pair SHEET would serve one battle in the game and leave both singles still wrong.** *The same move is owed to four more*: **`TWINS` two quails standing as two piglets ×8** (*Routes 8 and 14, Water Path, Bond Bridge*), **`YOUNG_COUPLE` two swans standing as a gazelle and an ox ×6**, **`SIS_AND_BRO` two rabbits standing as an axolotl and a duckling ×6**, **`CRUSH_KIN` two wolverines standing as a kangaroo and a wolverine ×4** (*half right already — `crush_girl` IS the wolverine; it is `black_belt`'s kangaroo that disagrees*). ***`SR_AND_JR` and `OLD_COUPLE` are NOT on this list***: *neither stands on a map, so neither is reachable.* **Method is `gencouple.py`'s — clear the heads, redraw on the portrait's own sixteen, assert the bodies came out byte-identical** ***All four drawn***: **`TWINS` two piglets, `YOUNG_COUPLE` an ox and a gazelle, `SIS_AND_BRO` a duckling and an axolotl, `CRUSH_KIN` a kangaroo and the wolverine it already had.** ***No colour was added, and that was CHECKED rather than assumed***: *the obvious move is to re-dye the indices the old head had to itself and there are **none** — all four heads draw from the same ramp as the body under them, so a re-dye would repaint the clothes.* **Each head is drawn inside the sixteen the picture already has.** ***The kangaroo took FIVE drafts and the lesson is an old one***: *two of them built the head WIDE, filling the wolverine's own width, and both read as a helmet with horns — on a wide flat skull any pair of uprights at the corners is a horn, which is now the **fourth** time that failure has cost this project time (the moth, the hedgehog, the honeybee, this).* **Measuring `BLACK_BELT`'s own portrait settled it: a kangaroo's head is a NARROW WEDGE — twelve columns against a twenty-column body — and its ears angle out from the crown rather than standing on the corners.** ***And the FEET are not a detail***: *a piglet on splayed quail feet is the same contradiction one figure down*, **so the twins get cleft trotters and the couple cloven hooves** (*the legs above them were already thin enough for any of these four*). **Every run asserts the bodies came out byte-identical; only the cleared boxes may change.** *`spritejoin.py` now reads a pair's note as a SET — membership, not equality — and all nine pairings report accounted for.* ***The one disagreement left in the game is T-127***
issues.subject: T-128 Four PAIR classes stand as two single sprites of the wrong animals

issues.description: ~~**`CUE_BALL` is a rhinoceros riding the boar's bike**~~ — ***Done 2026-09-16*** (`tools/genrhino.py`; engine `ec580dba9`) (*8 objects, Routes 16–18; the last disagreement `spritejoin.py` reports*). ***It is the one class in the batch whose stand-in is not 16×32***: **`biker.png` is 32×32, ten frames, and a MACHINE as well as a rider** — *the boar took SIX drafts and engine.md records why (handlebars standing clear of the body read as outstretched arms; the head-on wheel as a licence plate; every draft wider than the sprite it replaced until one was MEASURED against vanilla's own front frame).* **Giving the class a 16×32 sheet would take the bike off a trainer vanilla deliberately put in the gang, which is a design decision and not a redraw** — *so: a rhino on the bike at the biker's geometry, or a rhino on foot and the gang loses a rider, or leave it.* ***Undecided*** ***VANILLA SETTLED THE QUESTION THE TICKET LEFT OPEN***: **Routes 16–18 ARE Cycling Road, every trainer on them is a rider, and the class is the gang's muscle** — *giving the rhino a 16×32 sheet would have fixed the species by breaking the scene*, **so the rhino rides.** ***And the MACHINE is not redrawn***: *it is already ours and it cost six drafts*, **so the tool reads our own `biker.png` and replaces THE HEAD ONLY — jacket, frame, wheels and tail lights come through untouched and it asserts row by row that they did.** ***Which frames share a head is DERIVED***: *the ten hold three between them — front, back and side, each once standing and twice more shifted a row for the walk — measured by comparing every frame's head band against the three standing ones at each offset, so a sheet redrawn later cannot quietly fall out of step with a table.* **The head was built too wide twice before it was MEASURED against the boar it replaces** (*14 columns with the ears at 12–19, not the 20 the first drafts used, which overhung the bike*). ***A 32×32 sheet is cut 4×4 and CHECKED 4×4***: *`-mwidth 4 -mheight 4`, `overworld_frame(pic, 4, 4, k)`, `.size 512` with the 32×32 oam and subsprite tables, and a decode that reassembles sixteen tiles rather than eight* — **decoded 2×4 instead, frame 0 'fails', which is how five of the player's own sprites were once reported scrambled when nothing was wrong.** *`gentowns.register_one()` takes the geometry as a parameter now instead of hard-coding 16×32.* ***DISAGREEMENTS IN THE GAME: ZERO*** — **60 pairings agree over 414 objects and the nine pair-class pairings all report accounted for**
issues.subject: T-127 CUEBALL is a rhinoceros riding the boar's bike

issues.description: ~~**A trainer's battle portrait and their overworld sprite are different animals**~~ — ***Done 2026-09-16*** (`tools/genclasses.py`, `tools/gencouple.py`, `tools/genpsychic.py`, `tools/spritejoin.py`; engine `a3ddfaa77`, `50dcd7b66`, `e2a9a57b6`, `0b52e5ea3`) (*noticed on playtest 2026-09-16: "some trainer sprites (animals) didn't match their overworld sprites (animals)"*). ***The cause is vanilla's own sprite reuse and NOTHING here regressed***: **vanilla gives a Burglar the Poké Maniac's overworld sprite, a Juggler the Rocker's, a Breeder the Woman's** — *which was invisible while every one of them was a generic human.* **T-120's fable rule — "a class's portrait and its overworld sheet are one species" — made the reuse LEGIBLE, so a contradiction vanilla hid is now on screen.** ***Found by joining the engine rather than the tools' comments***: *742 trainers in `trainers.h` → 258 script labels that start a `trainerbattle` → the map object that runs each one*, **which gives 38 distinct (overworld sprite, battle portrait) pairings actually standing on maps.** *Five disagree, twelve trainers in all*: **POKE_MANIAC opossum stands for BURGLAR weasel ×3; ROCKER skunk for JUGGLER octopus ×3; WOMAN_2 ewe for POKEMON_BREEDER goose ×2; HIKER badger for RUIN_MANIAC aardvark ×2; and COOLTRAINER_M wolf ×1 and COOLTRAINER_F falcon ×1 both stand for COOL_COUPLE's two ibexes.** *A first pass reported the 47 CORPUS STAFF trainers as mismatched too and that was a FALSE ALARM — their portraits are drawn under the job names `corpus_m`/`corpus_f` rather than `p_rocket_grunt_*`, and both sides are the same penguins; a parser that keys on a naming convention finds a mismatch wherever the convention was not followed.* ***Decided 2026-09-16***: **the four single classes get overworld sheets of their own** (*weasel, octopus, goose, aardvark — all above T-120's ≥3-trainer cut-off at 7, 6 and 8 trainers, so they have earned drawings*), **and COOL_COUPLE, which is a PAIR class standing as two separate single sprites, has its portrait redrawn as the two animals it actually stands as — a wolf and a falcon** — **shipped: `burglar` (weasel), `juggler` (octopus), `pokemon_breeder` (goose) and `ruin_maniac` (aardvark), four NEW nine-frame sheets registered as their own `OBJ_EVENT_GFX_*`, and the ten objects that BATTLE as one of them repointed across seven maps** (*Poké Mansion 2F/3F/B1F, Silph 5F, Victory Road 2F, Pattern Bush, Lost Cave*). ***Each sheet inherits the SLOT of the sprite it replaces*** — *pink/2 from the maniac, blue/1 from the rocker, white/4 from the woman and the hiker* — **because the engine patches the palette named by a sprite's tag INTO the slot named by its info, so two sprites sharing a slot with different tags repaint each other**; *the palette was therefore already loaded on every map they stand on, each figure is drawn from the sixteen that slot already has, and no colour is added anywhere* (**engine.md trap 17**). **The couple's portrait is redrawn instead of given a sheet** — *a pair sheet would serve one battle in the game and leave the wolf and the falcon still wrong* — **and nothing below the collar changed: rows 0–23 hold head and nothing else, so the two heads are cleared and redrawn on the couple's own palette.** ***The falcon took four drafts and the fix was to TURN THE HEAD***: *a beak pointed at the viewer is a nose, the cheeks either side of it are a face, and every front-facing draft came out a person with a bowl cut* — **in profile the hooked wedge is a bird and nothing else.** *Verified by DECODE in all four ROMs, not by byte-match: a scrambled sheet matches its own scrambled self.* **Left open for T-120: the cooltrainer portraits themselves are still vanilla's purple-haired humans, and the 38-pairing join is the check that will close it** ***CLOSED TOO EARLY, AND THE REASON IS THE TICKET'S OWN LESSON WEARING DIFFERENT CLOTHES***: **the join globbed `data/maps/*/scripts.inc`, which holds 258 of the game's 726 battle labels** — *`data/scripts/trainers.inc` is ONE shared file holding 468 more, which is every route and island trainer there is.* **It did not fail. It reported 38 pairings where there are 72, five disagreements where there are sixteen, and the repointing that followed was a third of the job** (*engine.md **trap 18***). ***Widened and finished 2026-09-16***: **eleven more classes drawn and registered — `BIRD_KEEPER` an ostrich (18 objects, the largest disagreement in the game), `GAMER` a jackal (6), `SUPER_NERD` a lemur, `PAINTER` a toucan, `AROMA_LADY` a honeybee (4 each), `PSYCHIC_F` a jellyfish, `POKEMON_RANGER_M` and `_F` one pine marten in two uniforms (3 each), `LADY` a swan, `ENGINEER` a beaver, `TAMER` a hyena (2 each)** — *every one of their pictures already existed; what was missing was the sprite.* **60 more objects repointed, 16 sheets in all.** ***The honeybee came out a BULL first*** — *`mammal()` puts an ear at each top corner and two straight stalks over a tan face are horns, which engine.md had already recorded twice* — **so it is drawn without a mammal head: compound eyes taking the sides of the whole face, antennae two rows tall ending in a KNOB, which is what a horn never does.** ***And the portrait census was wrong in the other direction too***: *of the 79 still on vanilla art, **exactly ONE is reachable** — `PSYCHIC_M`, TRAINER_PSYCHIC_DARIO in the SEVEN ISLAND TRAINER TOWER, with a VS Seeker rematch; the other 78 are named in `trainers.h` and nowhere else.* **He is repainted from our own `psychic_f` rather than drafted** (*no tool here can post to `daemon/sprite`; this is `genbacks.py`'s method — keep the six colours that are the jellyfish, re-dye the nine that are cloth*), **and the first dye came out a bright rose because it lifted red; value is what the muted register is made of, so the second takes the ramp DOWN into an indigo.** ***`tools/spritejoin.py` is the check that should have existed first***: it prints **what it examined before what it found**, and its test is *names OR species* — *matching names alone reported 47 CORPUS STAFF trainers as mismatched, matching species alone reported every town's staff against itself.* **Disagreements: 16 pairings over 68 objects → ONE over 8. Left as T-127 and T-128**
issues.subject: T-126 A trainer's battle portrait and their overworld sprite are different animals

issues.description: ***LOGIC and INTUITION done 2026-09-16*** (`tools/genbacks.py`, second draft): **the method the first draft's failure named — TRACE VANILLA'S OWN FRAMES AS THE SKELETON AND REPAINT THEM — and all four of that draft's defects are gone**: *there is a head, there are shoulders and arms, the tail comes out from behind the coat, and the throw is visible, because the animation is vanilla's exactly rather than invented.* ***The palette does most of the work***: **vanilla's indices already carry roles** (*2/3/4 skin, 8 hair, 9/10 shirt, 5/6 jeans, 11/12 cap, 13/14 pack, 15 outline, 1 and 7 spare*), **so swapping the sixteen colours role for role changes the character without touching a single index.** *But a role-for-role swap gets the PROPORTIONS wrong — vanilla is mostly backpack (830px) over a small shirt (302px) and ours is a long cream coat with a dark satchel — so the **pack's area becomes the coat**, which is the big surface on a back, and vanilla's ball emblem is left dark, where it reads as the bag without being edited at all.* **Three shape edits, each derived rather than placed: the brim grown from the hat's own pixels so it follows the head tilt, the emblem left as the satchel, and the tail grown from the coat's own bottom edge.** ***A REAL BUG, AND 9.10 SETTLED IT***: **the two files carry the SAME sixteen colours but use them for different things** — *in `red` 11/12 are the cap (1425px); in `leaf` they are only a sunhat's band (210px) while 9/10 are a white hat and 4/8 are long hair (1978px)* — **so recolouring leaf by red's roles put a white hat on INTUITION.** *The fix is not a second index map but 9.10's own ruling: these are ONE figure, "two people, and the player picks the one they would rather be", whose only difference is the tail — so **both strips trace red's skeleton**, and leaf's long hair, which this character does not have, never arises.* ***Said plainly: it is not a monkey.*** *From behind it carries the character's MATERIALS — brown hat, cream coat, dark satchel, grey fur at head and hands, and the tail — on a human silhouette, because repainting cannot add a muzzle. It is strictly better than the vanilla boy in a red cap that shipped before it and it is not as good as the overworld sheets.* **Sizes asserted against the files on disk (5 frames, `0x2800`); strips and palettes byte-checked in all four ROMs.** ***STILL OPEN***: **the old man and the pokedude, who are not the player and have no species yet — a decision before drawing.** *`RS_BRENDAN` and `RS_MAY` stay vanilla under T-120's cut-off* — ***Closed 2026-09-17*** (engine `f222af7de`, `1fd7c761e`; `tools/genmentors.py`): **the last two back pics needed no species decision after all — the game had made both.** *The old man is an OLD IGUANA, because you meet him on CALLOW's elder sheet; the PokéDude is CRYSTAL CLEAR, a fox, because STREAM's host line and every demo's narration already name her.* **The iguana is repainted with derived edits** (*the profile smoothed so the face is a lizard's and not a green man's, a round eye, a gold dewlap hung from the chin*); **CRYSTAL's head is REPLACED, not recoloured** — *a gold bob is still a haircut, and the PokéDude's skin runs unbroken from face to shoulder* — **one fox head drawn once and placed at an offset the tool finds and asserts, since all 283 of the head's pixels move together.** ***The old man's line went with it***: *"That is my grandson presenting" contradicted the show the player had just watched*, **and now reads "I watched those when they were new. They have not changed. I have."** (*approved wording*)
issues.subject: T-123 LOGIC and INTUITION done 2026-09-16

issues.description: ~~**The FIGHTING DOJO is the ninth gym and nothing has touched it**~~ — ***Done 2026-09-16*** (`tools/gbainterior.py proof_hall`), **from a concept**: *a hall that proves, and certifies nobody.* ***BRAZEN is the bought city*** — *brass over base metal, "honestly itself… worth a fraction as much" (2009)* — **so the PROOF HALL is the BENCHMARK's trade in the cheaper metal**: *a boarded floor, a canvas mat where the gallery of mounts has gilt (T-111), two plain steel pillars with a single brass shoe each, chalk tallies in fives that nobody countersigns (SLATE's wall, T-105), **an empty bracket where every BENCHMARK mounts its gauge** — never removed, never installed — **and a plaque cast and never engraved.*** **The emblem is vanilla's own**: *the Master already says "do not take our emblem as your trophy", and it cannot be taken because **QED is not a MARK** — it is not among the eight on the trainer card.* ***The 9.23 clash is fixed in one line***: *"I am the LEADER here!" becomes "Nobody appointed me." — there is one leader to a town and it is BRAZEN's, and his own title is left alone because four other texts still call him the KARATE MASTER.* ***`gTileset_PewterGym` now has ZERO consumers***, which is what this ticket wanted; **53 blocks, 67 tiles, 0 collision changes.** ***AND THE NAME WAS NEARLY OVERWRITTEN***: **T-25 renamed this building to the PROOF HALL in 2026**, *it ships in four maps' text and in `gText_QuestLog_FightingDojo`, and CHANGELOG records a QED board outside where the other towns carry a MARK board* — **but the concept was drafted by checking the species, move, item and ability tables and the bible, found the word free, and proposed a different name entirely.** ***A building's name lives in the game's own map text, and that was never searched***; the tileset was written once as `gTileset_DryRun`, reverted, and rebuilt as `gTileset_ProofHall`. ***And the KARATE MASTER is THE REFEREE*** (*asked 2026-09-16: "it shouldn't be karate as that isn't daemon related"* — **which is T-25's own objection, left unfixed on the man while it was fixed on his building**). *A **referee** checks a proof before it is accepted **and** calls the points in a match, so it carries two readings at once as `BENCHMARK` and `CHECKPOINT` do — and vanilla's own "Judge!" and "One point!" stop reading as karate the moment he is renamed.* **It sharpens the concept rather than restating it: a referee says whether a proof HOLDS, and holds no power to certify anyone.** *It also sits with what already shipped — his students are `FORMALIST`s, `KARATE CHOP` is `REDUCE` ("a problem cut down to a smaller one"), his room ends in QED, and the two daemons he gives are AXIOMKICK and REBUTTAL.* ***The Gym next door already said the rest of it***: **"There used to be 2 BENCHMARKS in BRAZEN. The PROOF HALL next door lost its BENCHMARK status"** — *so "a hall that certifies nobody" was canon before the concept was drafted.* **Twelve strings across three maps** (*the hall, the Fan Club, the BENCHMARK*), *every anchor asserted to occur exactly once before anything was written, every line at or under vanilla's own 35-character maximum, and `DOJO` retired with him.* **Checked in both directions through `gbastr.py`: the new lines are in all four ROMs and `KARATE MASTER` is in none.** *Left alone deliberately: `LOCALID_KARATE_MASTER` and the `…FromKarateMaster` label, which are symbols no player reads, and `MOVE_KARATE_CHOP`, whose string is already `REDUCE`*
issues.subject: T-122 The FIGHTING DOJO is the ninth gym and nothing has touched it

issues.description: ***Done 2026-09-15 — the rows are given back*** (engine `86c9ce343`): **`gbaroofs.py` reads `upstream/master` now and refuses to block any cell vanilla left walkable, restoring the ones it had already blocked — 38 cells across six towns.** ***Flood-filling from the same seed, reachability matches upstream EXACTLY in all six***, *where before four towns were each short by the length of their blocked run.* **Original ticket: The roof pass closed a walkway in four towns** (*found on playtest 2026-09-15*). ***`gbaroofs.py` blocks the row FOUR above a BENCHMARK door*** (`ROOF_DY = -4`) **across the building's width, so the player cannot stand on our colonnade's roof** — *and its docstring claims "the row behind it stays open in every town, so no path closes."* ***That claim is false.*** **Flood-filling the walkable tiles against `upstream/master` from the same seed**: *CELADON loses 8 at (8,26)–(15,26), PEWTER 7 at (12,12)–(18,12), DOLDRUM 6 at (28,17)–(33,17), CALLOW 6 at (33,6)–(38,6); ARDOR and QUICKSILVER lose none, their runs being unreachable anyway.* **In every case the lost set is EXACTLY the blocked run** — *nothing beyond it becomes unreachable, so this is a walkway taken away rather than an area cut off.* ***And the row is ground, not roof***: **vanilla left it walkable with open ground above it and the building's own solid body below** — *it is the strip you walk along under an overhang.* **The pass is not wrong to exist** — *our colonnade draws a roof at that row, which is why the player appeared to walk out onto it* — **so the choice is: unblock those rows and accept the roof, or change the colonnade art so it stops drawing roof over ground the player may stand on.** ***A design call under 9.23, not a bug to squash quietly.*** *`engine.md` trap 15's lesson applies here too: the tool's own claim about its blast radius was never tested, and a flood-fill against upstream is what tests it*

issues.description: ~~**HELP could not be closed, and would have blacked out the overworld**~~ (*found driving the build in the theatre, 2026-09-21*) — ***DONE AND CLOSED 2026-09-21*** (engine; `start_menu.c`; T-179): **the START menu polls a chosen entry's callback EVERY FRAME until it returns TRUE**, *and T-179's HELP entry sets its request and returns FALSE* — ***so the request was set again on the frame the Help System closed, which re-opened it, forever.*** **B could not get out of HELP and neither could START; only a reset could**, and *this shipped in all four ROMs.* **Fixed by asking once and handing the menu back to `StartCB_HandleInput`** — *`main()` skips the game's callbacks while help is up, so the menu simply waits underneath, which is what the entry was written to do.* ***A second fault underneath it***: **HELP was absent from `StartMenu_FadeScreenIfLeavingOverworld`'s exception list**, *so picking it faded the overworld to black behind a screen that draws its own* — **exactly the bug the comment beside that list already describes for DEBUG**, which is the second time this list has cost a screen. ***Neither would have been found by building***: *both compile, and only pressing B shows either.*
issues.subject: T-182 HELP could not be closed, and would have blacked out the overworld

issues.description: ~~**The daemons' outlines are eighteen different blacks**~~ (*the user's, 2026-09-21, after T-177's true black reached the portraits and not the creatures*) — ***DONE AND CLOSED 2026-09-21*** (`tools/gbasprite.py`; 9.4 amended, v11.229): **measured off the screen rather than the file** — *a GROWTH daemon's outline reads `(24, 33, 24)`, a dark green.* ***9.4 kept a trace of the hue at level 0*** on the reasoning that **an outline that takes the hue stops reading as an outline**, *and the answer taken from that was "a trace is not the hue".* **It is** — *and across eighteen types it made eighteen blacks, none of which reads as black beside a portrait carrying the real one.* ***The lesson survives the reversal***: the guarantee is to give the outline no hue at all. **`ramp5` ends on `INK = (16, 16, 20)`, the same constant `gbaoutline.py` uses**, *so a daemon and the person throwing it are edged in one colour.* **454 sprites rewritten; the hue is carried by the three entries whose job it is.**
issues.subject: T-184 The daemons' outlines are eighteen different blacks

issues.description: ~~**The Index shows you a whole evolution line you have never met**~~ (*the user's, 2026-09-21: "only the daemons you have (own or seen) should be illuminated"*) — ***DONE AND CLOSED 2026-09-21*** (`pokedex_screen.c`; 4.2, v11.229): **`DexScreen_DrawMonPicInCategoryPage` draws the picture AND the name with no seen gate at all** — *only the caught ball is gated* — **and a category page groups an evolution line**, so *meeting the first of a chain showed the rest of it for free.* ***Checked against upstream before touching it: identical, so this is vanilla's own behaviour and not a regression of ours.*** **Vanilla already knows the rule and breaks it here**: *the list two screens away prints `gText_5Dashes` for an unseen daemon, and pressing A on an unseen one on this page already does nothing.* ***Ours repaints the loaded pic's palette to one ink*** — **`RGB(2, 2, 2)`, the same black T-184 just gave the sprites** — *so an unseen daemon is exactly its own outline filled in*, **names it `-----` in the game's own idiom, and keeps the number**, *because where a thing sits in the Index is not what binding one earns you.*
issues.subject: T-185 The Index shows you a whole evolution line you have never met

issues.description: ~~**A black line across four figures**~~ (*the user, playing the build 2026-09-21: "crystals sprite has a black line in her middle"*) — ***DONE AND CLOSED 2026-09-21*** (`tools/gbaoutline.py`): **`gbaoutline` splits every picture into 64-row frames because a BACK PIC is a strip of stacked 64×64 frames**, *and outlining a strip whole inks the seams where one frame's feet meet the next one's head.* ***The four intro pictures are 64×96*** — **one figure, not a frame and a half** — *so the split drew an outline straight across them at the cut.* **Rows 63 and 64 carried three times the dark pixels of any other row, in all four**: CRYSTAL, the player in both poses, and the rival. ***A strip's height is a MULTIPLE of 64***; anything else is one picture and is outlined whole. *The four restored from before the pass and redrawn — edge in the darkest four goes **43% → 100%**, seam rows ordinary again.* **`gbachar.py`'s own outline pass was checked and is clean**: it works on the cut cell, so it never had the seam.
issues.subject: T-184a A black line across four figures

issues.description: ~~**T-185's premise was wrong, and the gap was the point**~~ (*the user's field test, 2026-09-21: "if I have only seen the base evolution I do not see the silhouettes for other unseen evolutions and I thought I should"*) — ***DONE AND CLOSED 2026-09-21*** (`pokedex_screen.c`): ***I read the draw site and not the fill site.*** **`DexScreen_DrawMonPicInCategoryPage` has no seen-gate on the picture or the name, which is why T-185 called it a leak** — *but `DexScreen_GetPageMons` only puts a species on the page **if** `FLAG_GET_SEEN`, so the draw function is never handed an unseen one and T-185's silhouette was **dead code**.* ***What vanilla actually does is worse than a leak***: **an unseen daemon is dropped from the page and the survivors close up**, *so a page of four you have half-met looks like a page of two and says nothing about the rest.* **A category page holds a habitat group, which is usually one or two whole evolution lines** — *`Grassland` page 1 is RATTATA·RATICATE·SENTRET·FURRET, page 3 the whole NIDORAN♀ line* — ***so the gap IS the information: it says the line goes on.*** **The unseen are kept on the page now and the silhouette finally runs**: *a black shape, named `-----`, number intact, and opening one still refused as it always was.* ***Also answers the user's DEADLETTER / EXHAUST confusion***: **a page is a HABITAT group, not one chain** — *88 and 109 are two separate lines sharing a page, the way RATTATA and SENTRET do.*

THRASHING, which ends when the fight does, is a sawtooth with no letters** — *the difference in KIND drawn rather than stated, and the tag space kept for things that keep.* ***It also settles an accident***: **THRASHING's three letters are taken — `THR` is THROTTLED.** *It went in the three tiles `battle_interface.c` has said were unused since vanilla, so **nothing else in the sheet moves**; *the tool found the truth by refusing to map nibble 13.* ***The sheet gains a fourth row*** (`320x24 → 320x32`) **and all four battlers show the mark** — *safe because `gBattleInterface_Gfx` is declared `[][32]` and indexed by tile, and nothing anywhere counts them.*

issues.description: **A daemon carried on the companion evolves there; the game finds it already evolved** (*the user's C-184 choice, relayed by the companion session 2026-10-24, confirmed by the user here*). The game's half: (1) `companion_export.py` exports the evolution table (per species: method, parameter, target; the companion judges only level, friendship and time of day, never items or trades); (2) the save-side rule for SYNC -- the companion writes only the new species (and a renamed nickname if it was the default name), and the game finishes the evolution on load the way EvolutionScene does: stats recomputed, INDEX seen/caught set, moves learned at the new level offered, ability from the new species, Ninjask/Shedinja excluded; (3) a short "it changed while away" moment on return (DRAFT words, for the user). C-185 (a carried-only evolution method) waits on the user's bible decision. **The companion's half is built (companion ad9bce5, 2026-10-24).** It writes, besides C-184's species change, **one new HANDSHAKE** (species 261) per save, delivered on the first goal finished while a daemon is carried: a BoxPokemon in the PC's first empty box slot (never the party), with a fresh personality, the save's trainer id and name, nickname HANDSHAKE, AWAY bit set, exp for level 5, friendship 70, met level 5, metGame 4/5, Poke Ball, metLocation 0xFF, **no moves**, no EVs, and the marker (unusedRibbons bit 2). **So the load-time finish must walk the party AND every box** for the marker: give a daemon with no moves its level-up moves and PP, set the ability from abilityNum, mark the INDEX seen/caught, print metLocation 0xFF as the companion (BOUND / FIRST MET: a DRAFT line such as THE COMPANION), then clear the marker; party daemons also get CalculateMonStats. **Built (engine `888b17299`, 2026-10-24; the line it needed, T-450, in `5d9a9e16d`):** `src/daemons_carried.c` on Continue walks the party and all 14 boxes for the marker -- routines for its level with PP if it has none, abilityNum made one its species has, INDEX seen and caught, party stats recomputed, marker cleared; metLocation 0xFF reads **THE COMPANION** in BOUND, FIRST MET and the SUMMARY memo ("Met through THE COMPANION at Lv 5."); the first finished is said on the next step (after any dream): "Something followed you home from the / walk. X waits in the PC." (in the party: "X is with you."), or "X changed while it was / carried." -- all DRAFT, for the user. Proved in the theatre on a scratch save written by the companion's own `syncSave` gift (box 13, slot 27). C-184's evolved daemons get the same finish but no new routines offered (moves only for one with none).

issues.description: ~~**THE SUBTLE LAYER's three values, built**~~ **Built 2026-10-27 (engine 3d9e706f6); the user's answers the same day (engine 8efc0d0de): they wake only with THE SUBTLE LAYER (`FLAG_GOT_SUBTLE_LAYER`) -- before the book every battle is vanilla's, no read, write or leak -- and the tuning is approved as built (WRITE up to +10%, READ +3%/-2% a step, LEAK -5/-10%). DEBUG THE THREE's first row is the gate, "NOT YET: THE BOOK" until it is held, the values shown either way.** *Where they live: nowhere saved* -- each battle derives them per party daemon from friendship (CLOSURE; MAD 40+ takes one away) and T-431's feelings (ATTUNEMENT from CALM, VOLTAGE from the strongest feeling) and keeps them in `gBattleStruct`'s tail padding (heap, freed with the battle): 0 B of save, 0 B of release EWRAM/IWRAM, so the companion needs nothing. In battle a routine of no power raises ATTUNEMENT, joy, grief and a critical hit taken raise VOLTAGE, confusion and infatuation lower CLOSURE; for the player's own CONTEXT routines only, READ = A - V tunes accuracy, a WRITE (A x V) adds damage while CLOSURE holds, and a low CLOSURE with high VOLTAGE leaks; never in link battles. **Every number in one table (approved 2026-10-27): engine `include/daemons_three.h`**; `Three_ReadScore` is T-459 C's lean; DEBUG -> GAME EVENTS -> THE THREE views and sets them. *The book's wording, done 2026-10-27 (engine `edb60dfd8`, `0454701a2`): THE THREE opens "Every daemon carries three values", no longer "Trainers say", and ends "A daemon carries them as numbers it cannot see" -- the user dropped that line's "they say" too.* The ticket as filed: (*the user decided 2026-10-18 -- "per daemon, battle only" -- and filed 2026-10-24 reviewing the book: "soften now, ticket too"*): CLOSURE (how whole a daemon is), ATTUNEMENT (how thin its seam) and VOLTAGE (feeling in the moment), per daemon, **tuning CONTEXT routines in battle and never making a read come true in the world** (4.33). Where they live: **not the contest-condition bytes**, which T-431's feelings now hold (cool/beauty/cute/smart/tough and sheen: GLAD, MAD, SAD, CALM and the stamp), and not unusedRibbons bits 0-2 (the feelings and the companion's marker) -- *the game lane finds a free home before planning it (2026-10-24)*. The book's own formula is the spec: *reads rise with Attunement and fall with Voltage; writes need both, only while Closure holds*; what raises each is in THE THREE. **Until built, the book calls them trainer lore** ("Trainers say every daemon carries three values"); when built, drop the *trainers say* in `docs/subtle-layer.md` THE THREE and run `tools/gensubtle.py --write`.
issues.subject: T-454 THE SUBTLE LAYER's three values, built

issues.description: **The iPad app: the game's half** (*the user, 2026-10-24: "the iPad should be the ultimate app ... it should contain the game itself, the companion widgets, all from the iPad app ... u can download the game to your phone or tablet -- or companion ... first an iOS app -> tablet >> phone ... even just by getting the app you can plan the game, bring companions into your world, train/level them up"*). Decided: **grow daemons-companion's app** (the iOS lane owns it) into the hub, iPad first; **the game by patch, never bundled**: the user gives the app their own FireRed/LeafGreen ROM once, the app applies our BPS patch on the device and plays DAEMONS (the playground's EmulatorJS mGBA core, or a native mGBA core). **The game's half**: (1) publish each release's patches + hashes as data the app can fetch (romrelease/ghrelease, retail hashes to verify the user's ROM); (2) export **full INDEX cards with margins, coloured by the understandings gleaned** (species entries, OPUS margins, the understandings' flags and colours) for the app to draw from a save; (3) keep save and save-layout exports current; (4) whatever the app's planner needs (maps, routes, events). The app itself is a C- ticket for the iOS lane. **The user, later the same day**: *"one iOS app that combines the game / the companion / library / notebook ... so people can play, set the companion, without going too deep -- this self-contained system"* -- so the app is **self-contained**: the game, the companion (its server's logic inside the app, no hub or Mac needed), the LIBRARY and the NOTEBOOK in one install, simple to set up; the hub and the boards stay optional extras that pair with it. **Built (companion 854f214): index_cards.json and patches.json.** The user (2026-10-24): a card is coloured **by type match** -- grey until the understanding whose lobe shares one of the daemon's types is held, then its colour; daemons sharing no type colour on BOUND. **Planner data next**, in the iOS lane's order: (1) where each story event happens (map + rough spot) and their order; (2) how maps connect; (3) wild encounters per map; (4) trainers per map; (5) a level curve -- anything past the player's next step marked so the app can hide it; never the secrets or hidden books. ***PLANNER BUILT 2026-10-27 (DAEMONS, this commit; `tools/companion_export.py` `planner_tables`)***: *five files in the companion's `server/data/`, every record carrying `step` (how many story steps are done before it is reachable): `planner_story.json` (the attendant's 24 main-path steps, T-347, in the harness's order, each with its done flag and where it happens -- map, person/trigger/sign, x/y, ninth of the map), `planner_maps.json` (396 maps: place, type, size, edges, joins by warp/edge/script/ferry, the gate that holds each), `planner_wild.json` (both editions, day and night, land/water/smash/rods, slots summed per daemon), `planner_trainers.json` (253 trainers: class, name, party species and levels, beaten flag; rivals by starter; rematches after the story), `planner_curve.json` (per step: what opens, wild and trainer levels, the bosses). Reachability is a map-level walk through a hand-kept gate table (`PLANNER_GATES`); the tool refuses if a step's place opens after the step. Left out: the groves, THE NEXUS, BREATHVERSE, ARTSAI's station, NAVEL ROCK and BIRTH ISLAND, what is in DOLDRUM CAVE, hidden items, fixed encounters, every line of game text.* ***The user's answers (2026-10-27)***: *(1) the season, hour and weather homes stay out for now (`PLANNER_SHIFTS` False); (2) reveal up to the player's next step, as built; (3) trainers show daemons and levels only; (4) the planner's own words (gate reasons, four renamed step labels) are marked `draft: true` and await the user's approval. Islands 1-3 open after the HEAT MARK, as built.*

issues.description: ~~**Room for more object sprites**~~ (*the user, 2026-10-27: "widen the sprite numbering too"*): T-460 took OBJ_EVENT_GFX id 239, the last free one before the VAR graphics (240+); NUM_OBJ_EVENT_GFX is 240. Make room without breaking saves: graphicsId is a u8 in object event templates and live object events, some of which the save keeps -- so first prefer reclaiming ids vanilla defines but nothing in our game uses (link-only, e-Reader, Ruby/Sapphire leftovers), with a check that fails on any reuse; widen to u16 only if reclaiming cannot give enough, and only with the save impact measured and shown to the user first. Also fix tools/gentowns.py, which appends ids at NUM_OBJ_EVENT_GFX and would now collide with the VAR range. ***PART DONE 2026-10-27 (engine `3d467a371`)***: *three ids freed, no save touched: CAPTAIN (63, off the map since T-313), TRAINER_TIPS (104) and MEW (140) are placed, spawned, VAR-set and read by nothing and held by none of the 19 saves on this machine, so they became `OBJ_EVENT_GFX_FREE_<n>` (slots still on vanilla's art, listed on event_objects.h's `FREE:` line); both debug ROMs are byte-identical before and after. Not freed: 14-15 (Ruby/Sapphire link partners), 38 (TRAINER TOWER), 102 (FAME CHECKER), 148-150 (PROTEUS; 150 is gbaowslots.py's alias), and all sixteen VARs (240-255) are in use. `gentowns.register_one` (and so genrhino, genclasses, gencast, genhunter, gennamed, gentrainers) now takes the lowest FREE id and refuses to number into the VAR range; new `tools/check_objgfx.py`, run by check_lexicon, fails on a FREE id used, a shared number, a missing slot or a doubled colour row. **Waiting on the user: widening.** Three ids is short of the ~16 wanted. Measured: a u16 field would move the save's structs, but the bits are already there unused -- the template's pad byte at +3 (0 in all 64 templates of every save read), ObjectEvent bits 28-31 (0 in every save): a high byte there gives 12-bit ids with no layout change. The recap's QuestLogObjectEvent has no spare room (its 3 `unused` bits hold data in real saves), so the recap would have to skip or fold ids above 255.* ***DONE 2026-10-27 (engine `f020c9c9d`), phase 2, the user's decision: widened.*** *The id is 12 bits in bytes the save already had: its low byte where the u8 was, the high bits in the template's padding byte at +3 and ObjectEvent's bits 28-31 -- no struct moves (static asserts on both sizes and offsets). Read `OBJ_GFX_ID(p)`, write `SET_OBJ_GFX_ID(p, id)`. Ids: 0-239 as before, 240-255 the VARs (reserved), new sprites 256 (`OBJ_EVENT_GFX_WIDE_START`) to 4095 (`OBJ_EVENT_GFX_ID_LIMIT`); the table's 240-255 slots stay empty once it grows. Every function that takes an id is u16, `createvobject` takes a halfword, `object_event`/`clone_event` emit two bytes and refuse an id past the limit. **Saves unaffected:** the high bytes were 0 in all 48 readable saves on this machine (templates and live objects, including the two retail cart backups), so each reads the same id; all four ROMs' 1777 map templates match their map.json ids with +3 = 0. A probe build (id 256 on PALLET, then removed) emitted lo 0 / hi 1, filled table slot 256 and left 240-255 empty -- not run in an emulator. **The recap's stand-in:** the quest log keeps a u8, so a wide id is recorded as its row in `quest_log_objects.c`'s `sQuestLogGfxStandIns` (a like-shaped narrow id; `gentowns.register_one(..., stand_in=...)` adds it), else `OBJ_EVENT_GFX_QL_STAND_IN` (LITTLE_BOY, the engine's own fallback). `gentowns` takes FREE ids first, then 256 up; `check_objgfx.py` allows the wide range, fails on an id in 240-255 or past the limit, checks the stand-in rows and lists wide ids without one. Not done: engineAi's bridge reads the id as a byte.* |

issues.description: **The rest of the overworld art is still vanilla** (*the user, 2026-10-22: "we still have a lot of vanilla sprites, and they all need updating" -- buildings, tilesets, people, field objects*). The world was redrawn in CODE by the gba*/gen* tools (T-52, T-61-85, T-105-129); T-164 and T-170 found the sprite server cannot author tiles or reduce portraits, so code stays the method. **First a census**: every object-event sheet, trainer overworld, field effect, primary and secondary tileset (and its palettes), compared byte for byte with pristine pret/pokefirered -- what is ours, what is untouched vanilla, and where a player meets each untouched one first -- then batches in the order a player sees them, each on a contact sheet for the user before it is built (T-125's zero-collision-change rule). **Census 2026-10-22** (scratch t438/: census.py, census.json, sheets): **people and placed objects are 100% ours; 67.5% of all 8x8 tile draws are still Nintendo's.** Vanilla: 35 of 37 door animations, 45 of 51 field effects, 9 of 10 weather, primary/general's 428 remaining tiles (23.4% of draws), primary/building 99.9% vanilla (contradicts T-125's "already ours"), most caves, the town secondaries' leftovers (CALLOW 46% .. FUCHSIA 99%), the island towns. Proposed batches A doors + arrow, B field effects + weather, C general ground, D interiors, E caves, F town leftovers, G endgame and ships; leave out pokemon_tower and the 21 unplaced tilesets. **The user, 2026-10-22:** order A doors (BLANCHE's first) -> B field effects and weather -> C the general ground, then the rest; interiors: redraw primary/building IN PLACE (every interior at once, collision never moves, one big contact sheet first); caves: a look per cave matched to its name; the unplaced sprites and tilesets were shown to the user, who may use some -- any chosen gets redrawn (people as animals). **Batch A drafted 2026-10-22** (`tools/gbadoors.py`, gfx/drafts/t438/doors/, DAEMONS 43f82681; sheets qa 22Oct T438): 30 door animations + the door-mat arrow. **The user approved all as drawn and the double-chevron arrow, and asked to fix: OAK's lab door (gbalab.py --door) whose knob stays while the door opens; the general door's palette row (2 -> 5: today a gold door opens teal); cable_club and dept_store_elevator palette rows; the tiles 376-383 overlap on CHECKPOINT 2F (block 0x303) and SAFFRON (0x392) that leaves door frames after a door opens.** **Batch A BUILT 2026-10-22 (engine b3cc6cb50)**: `gbadoors.py --write --approved` -- 30 doors and the double-chevron arrow; field_door.c rows set by the tool (general 5; cable_club 7,7,9,9,9,9,9,9; lift 7,7,7,7,11,11,11,11); the cable club door's lone row-7 tile re-indexed into row 9 so its open room is one colour; the lab door's handles slide away with its leaves (`gbalab.py --door`); nothing draws tiles 376-383 any more -- CHECKPOINT 2F's pots (0x303-0x305) on primary/building's unused slots 262-266 (none free in its own tileset; batch D must keep them), BRAZEN's 0x392/0x393 in four saffron_city slots freed with nothing on screen changed. Walked in the theatre (`tools/routes/doors.json`, CONTENT and a CONTEXT subset); after a door played, VRAM's tilemaps held no entry on 1016-1023. **Batch B drafted 2026-10-22** (`tools/gbafieldfx.py`, gfx/drafts/t438/fieldfx/, DAEMONS 0d1dea2e; sheets t438b_fx_1-7, t438b_weather_1-2): shadows, dust, PRUNE's sprig, ripple, sand prints (monkey feet), bike tracks, splashes, REVEAL's sparkle, KETTLE SPRING water, streaks, the RECORD monitor (the CHECKPOINT cartridge), THE ANNEX shards, rain, snow, horizontal fog; general_0.pal's dust and sand entries move onto our ground. Dead effects (bird, ash, disguises, cloud/ash/bubble weather) left. Waiting on the user: approve; dead sheets; monkey prints for all; the streak banner's black; a warmer fog; the RECORD symbol. Its --writes sandbox run saw 1 new drift while the doors build had the engine mid-edit -- re-run on a quiet tree. **Batch C drafted 2026-10-22** (`tools/gbageneral.py`, gfx/drafts/t438/general/, DAEMONS d41f8dc2): a surface pass on rock (weathered slabs), ledges, sand ripples, dirt, cobbles; fences, bushes, hedges, the blue house and the SAFFRON GYM sign barely touched (need motifs); no palette change. My read: ROUTE 1/2 barely change and ROUTE 3's rock reads flatter and noisier than vanilla's scales -- probably a second pass. Waiting on the user. **The user, 2026-10-22: batch B approved as drawn** (monkey footprints for everyone, the RECORD shows the CHECKPOINT cartridge, default fog); **batch C: a bolder second pass** -- rock that reads as solid stone with a look of our own, and motifs for fences, bushes, hedges and the blue house -- then show again. **Batch C pass 2 drafted 2026-10-22** (DAEMONS 4ed5f619; t438c2_*): lit tops and layered faces, our own motifs. **The user: the motifs approved with the ribbed roof (fences, bush, hedge, signboard, gym sign); the rock to a third pass -- chunkier stone, big irregular blocks and boulders over the lit-top/dark-face planes, so it reads as rock, not planks** (palette unchanged unless the third pass shows a reason). **Batch C pass 3 drafted** (DAEMONS a17cf836; t438c3_*): chunky stone, the 112/114/179/113 seams fixed, today's palette. **The user approved it, 2026-10-22: build batch C** (pass 3 rock + the approved motifs with the ribbed roof). **Batch C BUILT 2026-10-23 (engine `7d3697878`, and `4534997ae`: the grove bush's tell redrawn from the new bush by gbagrove.py)**: `gbageneral.py --write --approved` -- 218 tiles in primary/general's tiles.png and the two water-edge strips (pass 3 rock, the motifs with the ribbed roof, sand ripples, cobbles, dirt); no metatile, collision, behaviour or palette moved, every PNG 4-bit 16-colour, gbaseams.py unchanged (541 cells, all secondary). SMOULDER, THE DOTS, UMBRAL ASCENT (split). **The user approved all; OTHER CAVE's light changes on each entry, in a learnable cycle of four, and its wild daemons follow the light (VAR_ALTERING_CAVE_WILD_SET); THE DOTS' braille says "hi"; touch up SMOULDER's ash tops and THE DOTS' top dots before building.** **Batch E BUILT 2026-10-23 (engine `2007d739f`, and `e2f7eea4f`: OTHER CAVE's cycle)**: `gbacaves.py --write --approved` -- all eleven looks; SMOULDER's tops now lie in ash drifts, THE DOTS' top braille ("hi") reads at 1x; every tile drawn over vanilla's, so a second write is a no-op; no metatile, attribute, collision, behaviour or map block moved, every PNG 4-bit 16-colour, DOLDRUM CAVE and HALFTONE untouched. issues.description: **`the foe` is vanilla's word for a thing** (*the user's, 2026-09-21, out of T-181: "'them' could be used for most of them if it buys a bit more and allows a better writing"*). ***It does both.*** **`the foe` is 40px and `them` is 23px**, and the saving is not the argument — *this game spends forty hours insisting the thing across from you has an inside, and `them` asserts that in every routine description a player reads without ever saying the thesis (craft rule 1).* **135 occurrences in `move_descriptions.c` and ten in everything else**, *so finishing the job costs almost nothing once it is started.* ***The catch is the prize***: **most are vanilla's PASSIVE** — *"The foe is hit with an intense flame"* — **and a blind swap writes "Them is hit with"**, so each has to be turned ACTIVE: *"Hits them with an intense flame"*, **132px → 93px, and better English.** ***So it is ~135 sentences of writing and not a regex***, which is why it is a ticket. **T-181's fourteen are done this way already** and three of them came back to T-138's own wording with only the pronoun changed. ***Closes when*** *no player-facing routine, ability or battle line calls a daemon `the foe`, a tool FLAGS each passive rather than rewriting it, and `port_vocab` still reports zero.* `engineGba/src/move_descriptions.c`, `tools/` — ***DONE AND CLOSED 2026-09-22***: **154 routine descriptions, six ability descriptions and the help system.** *Zero `foe` left in anything a player can read, zero lines over the 113px pane.* ***The 37 passives were turned ACTIVE by hand***, *which is why it is a table and not a regular expression* — **and why they read better afterwards: an active sentence is shorter, and these have four lines to live in.** ***THEN THE OUTPUT HAD TO BE READ, TWICE***, **which is the finding**: *a rule that turns "the foe" into "them" writes* **"takes what them was holding"**, *and a rule that leaves "it" alone writes* **"holds it there"** *about a someone it has just called them.* **Singular they needs the verb to agree AND the other pronouns in the sentence to follow it, and neither is something a substitution can know.** *19 found on the first read, 7 more on the second —* ***"Copies the routine them last ran" survived the first scan because "last" is not a verb a pattern thinks to look for*** — *and six say `foe` with no article at all ("all foe", "Prevents foe from"), which is vanilla's clipped plural and matches no rule.*

custom_fields.value: ***Built 2026-09-15 — all ten towns*** (`tools/gentowns.py`): **each town's generic citizens are its locals — a child, an adult and an elder — as new object graphics `OBJ_EVENT_GFX_TOWN_<TOWN>_<ROLE>`, all three sharing ONE palette of the town's own in `PALSLOT_NPC_SPECIAL`** (*tags 0x1120–0x1122*): *CALLOW a tree frog, a parakeet and an old iguana in greens, yellow and sky; SLATE a pangolin, a rock hyrax docent and an old armadillo in stone, slate and chalk; DOLDRUM a seal pup, a sea otter and an old walrus in pale sea, navy and ivory.* **The tool registers everything idempotently and repoints the citizens: the pilot's 52 (14 CALLOW, 22 SLATE, 16 DOLDRUM), then 144 more — 19 ARDOR, 15 HALFTONE, 52 VERDIGRIS, 23 LURID, 22 BRAZEN, 10 QUICKSILVER, 3 UMBRA — 196 citizens on 72 maps, on palette tags 0x1120–0x1129.** ***Left alone: DOLDRUM's city map, where AL shares the special slot (6 citizens).*** *Three read wrong at sixteen pixels and were redrawn: the armadillo was pink and read as a pig, the otter's all-sand face as a person's, the walrus as a man with a moustache.* **Species chosen for all ten towns 2026-09-15**: *ARDOR a red panda, a gull dockhand and an old rooster; HALFTONE a dalmatian, a zebra and an old panda; VERDIGRIS a gecko, a peafowl and an old heron; LURID a flamingo, a mandrill and an old cockatoo; BRAZEN a lion cub, a golden retriever and an old hamster; issues.description: **The third book's gate leaves the public writing** (*the user, 2026-10-31, by multiple choice, from the review of the three books and the story threads: "Yes, file it"*) Public writing tells THE HERMETIC LAYER only as rumour -- myth and real history, never how it is reached. Three places say more: the player's manual (`docs/manual/manual.md:843-844`, two lines: [private: vision-unredacted 4.39]); the bible (`vision.md:38`, the one exception's sentence, and 4.39's gate, with `:8975-8976` in the log); and `docs/books/README.md:15` ("People who have read both books sometimes talk about a third one"). Soften the manual and the README to rumour, print the manual again, and move the gate's detail out of the public bible into `docs/private/vision-unredacted.md`, leaving `[private: ...]` where it stood, as the four secrets are kept. What stays public by necessity: the engine's code and the book's own text (`docs/hermetic-layer.md`, which the build reads) -- this keeps the gate out of what people read, not out of reach. ***The manual's two lines are kept for now*** (*the user, 2026-10-31, asked whether to take them out: "no it is fine to keep for now, log it as a question later"*): **whether the player's manual keeps those two lines is an open question for the user, not yet part of this job** -- the quick start and micro start (T-507, T-508) carry neither line. ***DONE 2026-11-16 (bible v11.377)***: *`docs/books/README.md` now tells the third book only as rumour; the gate's detail -- 0.1's "said to be found late", 4.39's "the gate is hard" and "Two ways in", the 2026-10-29 log line and `docs/daemons-review-4.md`'s table cell -- moved to `docs/private/vision-unredacted.md` 4.39, each place reading `[private: vision-unredacted 4.39]`. The manual's two lines are untouched and stay the user's question, now in the bible's Open log.* ***The manual softened too, 2026-11-16 (bible v11.379)***: *the user, by multiple choice: "Soften to rumour". The two lines now read "Nobody agrees how it is found, or whether it is found at all." (DRAFT); the manual printed again.*
