issues.description: **The tarot decks in both books, app and GBA** (*the user, 2026-11-01, by multiple choice and in their own words; T-483 part (6)*) **Where**: a CARDS section in each book, **collapsed at first** -- the book opens on its cover page, and under it a tile that looks like a tarot deck, intuitive to press, expands it (and collapses it again). Both books. **Which deck**: each book has two kinds of card and, for every mode, the reader chooses *The Deck of Reason*, *The Deck of Instinct*, or *A Combined Deck* (THE SUBTLE LAYER); THE HERMETIC LAYER the same with its own two: ***The Deck Above & The Deck Below*** (*the user, 2026-11-01: "straight from 'as above, so below'"*) -- **The Deck Below**: bottom-up, logic, time; earth, the fixed, the sequential; things down here take time, the stone built brick by brick. **The Deck Above**: top-down, creativity, emotion, free association; the heavens, the timeless, the pattern that descends whole before you understand it. **The selector reads with words between the titles** (titles bold, the between-words not): *as **The Deck Above**, so **The Deck Below**, or **Both as One***; and in the thin half-hour it changes to *as **The Deck Within**, so **The Deck Without**, or **Both as One*** (*the user, 2026-11-01: the as / so / or and the commas are all the plain words; the frames ABOVE and BELOW approved as drawn, gfx/drafts/t509_cards/ round two*). Each of the 22 cards gets an ABOVE and a BELOW face, replacing C-239's single SPELLCRAFT face; THE THIRTEEN stays Halloween's card. **Expanded**: a card face down with *THE CARD OF THE DAY* above it; pressing it turns it over (fixed for the day, arcana.ts cardOfDay exactly). Beside it the modes: **the card of the day, a single draw, PAST / PRESENT / FUTURE, and MIND / BODY / SPIRIT** (the user's fourth). Choosing a mode clears the previous one; the deck shuffles and spreads; **the backs never show the card's type**; the reader touches a place in the spread and one card comes out from there, the deck moves away and the card is laid face down on a board -- a three-card mode has three bordered places labelled beneath (PAST / PRESENT / FUTURE or MIND / BODY / SPIRIT) and three cards are chosen. **Effect**: only read. **Art**: the card's daemon sprite on drawn frames (REASON circuit, INSTINCT gold net, SPELLCRAFT emerald on the pulse), shiny 1 in 16; frames drafted on a sheet first. **The words (the user)**: each face has **two texts** (*the user, 2026-11-01: "a short version and then under that prophecy but that's only on the iOS apps"*) -- **the phrase**, a short line (38 characters at most) on the card's face, the game's and the watches'; and **the prophecy**, two or three sentences like the user's *universe* cards -- prophetic and metaphorical, drawing on the card's daemon, its type and its INDEX entry, turned by the book and the deck -- shown **only in the companion app**, under the card. Both live in the companion's arcana.json ({ keyword, phrase, prophecy, species }, C-272); the GBA prints keyword and phrase and needs no page for words. DRAFT. **Built twice**: the app by touch (the phone lane / THE SUBTLE LAYER session), the GBA by D-pad (the game lane: A opens the deck tile, left/right picks a mode and a place, A draws). Test vectors for the day's card: scratchpad vec.mts (RED12345 2026-11-01: subtle XVIII DREAMING, spellcraft XX INVOCATION).

custom_fields.value: ***DEFERRED 2026-09-26 by the user*** *until the local AI hardware arrives and the RAM budget is clearer.* ***The only one of the five ideas with a real RAM cost.*** It wants an object-event slot and sprite tables, and `engine.md` puts the free static space at **1.1 KB of EWRAM and 2.9 KB of IWRAM**. **Measure it before promising it** — every other job on this list is ROM-only and free. *Deferred 2026-09-10, by choice rather than by blocker* ***MEASURED 2026-09-23, and RAM is not the cost.*** **RAM**: *a follower is one of the 16 object-event slots plus a few bytes of state — against 804 B of EWRAM and 2.9 KB of IWRAM free (`gbabudget.py`; this row's 1.1 KB is from September 10).* **Slots**: *16 object events including the player, and objects spawn only near the camera; 16 of 433 maps hold 14 or more templates (KINDLE ROAD 29, ROCK TUNNEL B1F 26), so those are where a crowded screen could refuse one.* **Palette**: *object events own 12 fixed slots (player, four NPC, one special, and a reflection for each); in BLANCHE one of the other four held a field tag and three were free, read live from `sSpritePaletteTags` — so a follower loads its type colour by tag, the way field effects do, with weather and emotes as its only rivals.* ***ART and ROM are the cost.*** **42 overworld daemon sheets exist, all vanilla, and 26 are three still 16×16 frames — no walk.** *A follower needs about nine frames (three facings, two steps each) per daemon:* **at 16×16 that is 1.1 KB each, ~270 KB for the 240 named daemons; at 32×32 it is 4.6 KB each, ~1.1 MB.** ***CORRECTED 2026-09-25: the ROM has ~6.8 MB free, not ~1.3*** *— the graphics block is pinned at retail's 0x08D00000 and the high-water mark counted the 5.5 MB gap below it as used; the 1.3 MB was only the tail after it (engine.md, the three memories). So both sizes fit; the choice is the art's cost and the look, not the space.* *So the promise is a SPRITE job the size of the bestiary.* ***WAITING ON THE USER:*** whether to start the follower, and at 16×16 or 32×32 — asked on the private field-test page, Questions for you → “A daemon walking behind you (T-18)”. ***PLANNED AND DECIDED 2026-10-20 (the user, by phone; docs/private/plan-follower-2026-10-20.md)***: *no new art -- the follower is the lead's own 2-frame party icon, a 1px hop for the bob, flipped for right; in its TYPE colours (a per-species palette remapped from its front sprite, ~13 KB), greyed by friendship as T-424; 1x, a tile behind; the first daemon that is not an egg, HALTED or AWAY; follows on the bike, with an OPTIONS toggle to switch it off. journals.notes: The user, 2026-11-18: each daemon's page shows a staff -- the clef, its type's key signature, its song's notes -- with the quotation; the notes coloured, and the sharps and flats of the key signature coloured too, "so the visual pattern can also teach you the key"; each type's section names its key's letter, major or minor, its key signature and the key's colours.

**The plan, ready for the moment T-599's styles are picked** (*lane story, 2026-11-22, the day's goal loop; nothing written yet, no quotation before the picks*).

**What the book is**: THE COLOURS WITHIN THE WORDS (working title), a book of quotations. Its preface connects CALLOW SCHOOL's lesson on language across code and music: a daemon's essence has a voice, a song, a language and a quotation (said through the sections, never as the thesis). Then one section for each of the 18 types, in the engine's type order and its song's key as `docs/quotations-draft.md` sets them (CONTENT C major ... OPAQUE B minor).

**A section** opens on its type's key: the key's letter, major or minor, and its key signature on a staff. Its sharps and flats are drawn in the key colours, so the pattern teaches the key (the user, 2026-11-18). The section's colours are the key's. Then a short paragraph on the type's style of quotation, from the picked style.

**A daemon's page**: its number and sprite, its quotation in large quote marks, and a staff with its type's clef and key signature carrying its song's notes, coloured.
- The writing is "almost handwritten in the penmanship of the daemon"; every daemon of a type writes in the same hand.
- Order within a section is by INDEX number. A line's forms are read in order if question 4 is picked A.
- A dual-type daemon is filed under its first type if question 5 is picked A.

**What it reuses** (no new pipeline):
- `tools/gensongs.py`: each daemon's key and notes.
- `tools/genplaynotes.py` KEYS: the twelve note colours C..B, the same ones the companion exports as key_colours.
- `companion/server/data/species.json`: numbers, sprites and the quotation once T-599 writes it.
- `tools/manual.py`: the PDF, gaining a `--book quotations` beside the others.
- The game's books, through `tools/gensubtle.py`, as another open book. Whether the game carries all ~400 pages or a reader's selection is a size question, to measure first.
- The companion's LIBRARY, its pages read from the same JSON.

**Its own work, in order, after the picks**:
1. The hands: one penmanship per type, drawn as fonts or glyph sets. The PDF can use the hand freely; the GBA's is limited to its glyph widths, so measure before promising.
2. The staff drawing: clef, key signature, notes, in both PDF and companion.
3. The preface, DRAFT, read by the user.
4. The PDF printed. Then the companion's LIBRARY. Then the game, with its size measured first.
5. A voice, chosen with the user from samples (T-543); the audio gate fails every release while a printed book has none.

**Waiting on**: T-599's picks; nothing else.

journals.notes: Claimed by lane-story on shadow-book.

The book's own lessons are a broom put back, not broken, and an orphaned routine adopted by 'the first process of all' -- and the old man on the tower's top floor is INIT. The book never names him.

Game version drafted (branch shadow-book, 042907ec): docs/shadow-book.md, 24 entries, measured by gensubtle --book shadow. Still to do: its 24 pictures for the reader's 16 colours, cover and icon, BOOK_SHADOW in book_reader.c and its item; and the exact spot in the tower (asked).

issues.description: **The playground plays a cached older ROM after every release** (*the playground lane, found while building E-3, 2026-11-20*): EmulatorJS 4.2.3 keeps a ROM it has played in IndexedDB (EmulatorJS-roms) under its file name alone -- daemonsContent.gba -- and plays that copy again whenever the server's Content-Length matches (emulator.js downloadRom); every DAEMONS ROM is 16,777,216 bytes, so a browser that once played in the playground keeps playing that ROM after each new release (seen in the cache 2026-11-20 while building E-3; the release in the URL path does not reach the key). Fix: key EmulatorJS's copy by release and clear the older ones, or hand it the ROM as a File, as E-3's carts are; then check a tester's browser plays the newest.

journals.notes: Claimed by lane-playground on main.

Seen first, then fixed, 2026-11-21, on a throwaway playground with two real releases: with v11.411.1 the newest the page said v11.411.1 and EmulatorJS ran its stored copy of v11.409 (CRC 1B7BDE75 for FBB9C962). The ROM's address now ends in the release (…/daemonsContent.gba?v11.411.1), which EmulatorJS's cache key keeps and its file name and save drop, so saves still carry across releases; every other copy of that build is deleted before a game starts. After: v11.411.1 loads FBB9C962, and switching back loads 1B7BDE75, one copy kept each time. Live on 4740 at once (the page is read from disk): a tester's stale copy goes at their next PLAY.

**A question for the user** (*lane playground, 2026-11-23*): How far may an agent's sandbox reach? (files, network, repos)

Choices:
- NARROW: a fresh worktree of the public repos only (eudaimonia, companion, praxis); network only to the tailnet (Redmine, EUDAIMONIA, the hub) and the model's API; it pushes a branch, never main
- MIDDLE: worktrees of every repo it is given a ticket in, DAEMONS and the engines included but never docs/private/; tailnet + GitHub + npm + the model's API; it pushes a branch and opens a PR
- WIDE: its own user on roverbyteseer with every repo; any network; it may push main after its checks pass, as the sessions do today
- READ ONLY first: it may read the repos and the tickets and write only notes and WORKING MEMORY, until it earns more

**The user's answer** (2026-11-23, by multiple choice): **MIDDLE** -- worktrees of every repo it holds a ticket in (DAEMONS and the engines included, never docs/private/); tailnet + GitHub + npm + the model's API; it pushes a branch and opens a PR.

NETWORK: one connection, to the runner's proxy, which forwards only to GitHub, npm and the model's API on 443/80 and the tailnet (a name only if it looks up to 100.64/10, connected by that address). OUT: after it stops, the runner fetches the branch alone into a clean bare copy and pushes from there (a hook or config the agent planted never runs outside), then opens a PR with gh (or finds the open one). Only variables named by --pass reach it. Proved end to end with a probe agent: every wall held (secrets, docs/private, other repos, the real repo, launchctl, example.com and a direct connection all refused; GitHub, npm and Redmine on the tailnet reached), its commit went out as the branch alone to a stand-in remote, its planted pre-push hook never ran. - Copied to roverbyteseer's DAEMONS checkout, all gitignored there as here (checked: 0 tracked changes): ROM RELEASE/CART BACKUPS (the user's cart backups and saves, mode 700) and the newest release v11.413.3's two ROMs (SHA-1s match the laptop's) and PATCHES/.
- The player runs there: launchd **ca.codemusic.eudaimonia-player** (server/playground.py --port 4740 --no-companion, Homebrew python3). Over the tailnet the egg now plays in full (roverbyteseer:4741 framing roverbyteseer:4740).
- From away: daemons-eudaimonia **07e27e7** gives the player a public name of its own, **play.daemons.codemusic.ca** (PLAYGROUND_PUBLIC_HOSTS; taken only with a proxy's hops), the dashboard tells a public page that address (EUDAIMONIA_PUBLIC_PLAYER, frame-src), and the player's page takes a cart only from the dashboard's public origin. Checked on roverbyteseer through the Mac mini's address: 200 by the public name via the proxy, 403 without the hops, 403 for a look-alike. 83 tests pass.
- **Waiting:** the user adds CNAME play.daemons -> codemusic.ca at WHC; then the Mac mini gets a vhost for it **behind the same Apache password** (the player serves release ROMs, which must never be public) and the certificate gains the name.
- **Still to do:** each new release's ROMs and PATCHES reach roverbyteseer only when copied; the slim DAEMONS checkout's hourly pull (ca.codemusic.daemons-slim-pull, added today) brings only the tracked notes.

**Public, 2026-11-23**: the user added CNAME play.daemons; the Mac mini has /etc/apache2/other/daemons-play.conf (-> 10.0.0.136:4740, Host preserved, WebSockets, **the dashboard's Apache password in front**); certbot's codemusic.ca lineage expanded to 20 names (dry run first). Checked: play. and dashboard. answer 401 without the password over a verified certificate; codemusic.ca unchanged. A browser asks for the password once per name, so open https://play.daemons.codemusic.ca once before the egg's frame can load it. **Left on this ticket:** each new release's ROMs and PATCHES reach roverbyteseer only when copied (v11.413.3 is there).

**Releases sync themselves, 2026-11-23** (the user: "please automate syncing new releases to roverbyteseer"): **tools/egg_sync.sh** (DAEMONS f6bb77bc), run hourly on the laptop by the login agent **ca.codemusic.egg-sync** (log ~/Library/Logs/egg_sync.log). It carries the newest release's two ROMs and PATCHES/, and ROM RELEASE/CART BACKUPS when they change, to roverbyteseer's slim DAEMONS checkout over the tailnet -- only files git ignores there as here (it refuses anything else) -- checks the ROMs' SHA-1s after, prunes roverbyteseer's older release ROMs to the newest three, and stops quietly when roverbyteseer is out of reach. First run: v11.413.3 already there. With this the ticket's last part is done.

issues.description: **PRIVATE MERGES: the dashboard's in-house merge tool for private files in conflict** (*the user, 2026-11-25*): When the private-file sync (T-636, Syncthing) finds a file changed on both machines, the dashboard shows a button with the count of private merge conflicts; clicking it signs you in if needed and opens a modal (with a full-screen option) listing the files in conflict. Pick one: like git, take either side whole, or tick the parts you want on each side to build a preview of the merged file in a third pane, which can also be edited by hand. Save, and you return to the list for the next. Admin only, signed in; the files' words never reach a public page or a log. Each machine is labelled by its name (DAEMONS-roverbyteseer and DAEMONS-M2cBook, labels only: the folders keep their names).
